sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第286卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 286
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 286

sentences.zh: 【後漢紀一】 起強圉協洽正月，盡四月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: [Later Han Records 1] Beginning in the first month of the year Qiangyu Xiejia, ending in the fourth month, less than one full year.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Han Records 1] Spanning from the first month of the sexagenary year Qiangyu Xiejia through the fourth month—less than a full year.

sentences.zh: 高祖睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝上天福十二年（

translations.literal: The late Emperor Gaozu, sagely in culture, martial in holiness, illustrious and solemn in filial piety, in the twelfth year of Tianfu (
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor Gaozu, posthumously styled Sagely in Culture and Martial in Holiness, Illustrious, Solemn, and Filial—in the twelfth year of the Tianfu era (

sentences.zh: 丁未，公元九四七年）

translations.literal: dingwei, CE 947)
translations.idiomatic: dingwei, 947 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁亥朔，百官遙辭晉主於城北，乃易素服紗帽，迎契丹主，伏路側請罪。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the month dinghai, the hundred officials took leave of the Jin emperor from afar north of the city, then changed into plain garments and gauze caps, welcomed the Khitan emperor, and prostrated themselves by the roadside to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (dinghai), the officials bade farewell to the Jin emperor from a distance north of the city, then put on plain dress and gauze caps to welcome the Khitan emperor, kneeling by the road to plead for mercy.

sentences.zh: 契丹主貂帽、貂裘，衷甲，駐馬高阜，命起，改服，撫慰之。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor wore a sable cap and sable fur coat with armor beneath, halted his horse on a high mound, ordered them to rise, change their dress, and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor came in sable cap and coat, armor underneath, and reined up on a height. He told them to rise, change clothes, and reassured them.

sentences.zh: 左衛上將軍安叔千獨出班胡語，契丹主曰：「汝安沒字邪？

translations.literal: Left Guard General An Shuqian alone stepped forward from the ranks speaking Khitan language. The Khitan emperor said: "Are you not An Mozi?
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General An Shuqian alone stepped out of the ranks and spoke in Khitan. The Khitan emperor said, "Aren't you An Mozi?

sentences.zh: 汝昔鎮邢州，已累表輸誠，我不忘也。」

translations.literal: You once governed Xing Prefecture and repeatedly submitted memorials pledging loyalty—I have not forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: You once held Xing Prefecture and sent memorial after memorial pledging loyalty. I have not forgotten."

sentences.zh: 叔千拜謝呼躍而退。

translations.literal: Shuqian bowed in thanks, shouted with joy, and leapt back.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqian bowed his thanks, cried out with joy, and bounded back to his place.

sentences.zh: 晉主與太后已下迎於封丘門外，契丹主辭不見。

translations.literal: The Jin emperor with the empress dowager and those below them went out to welcome him beyond the Fengqiu Gate; the Khitan emperor declined and would not see them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor, the empress dowager, and the court went out to welcome him beyond the Fengqiu Gate, but the Khitan emperor refused to receive them.

sentences.zh: 契丹主入門，民皆驚呼而走。

translations.literal: When the Khitan emperor entered the gate, the people all cried out in alarm and fled.
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitan emperor entered the gate, the populace screamed and scattered.

sentences.zh: 契丹主登城樓，遣通事諭之曰：「我亦人也，汝曹勿懼！

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor ascended the city tower and sent an interpreter to announce to them: "I too am a human being—you must not fear!
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor climbed the city tower and had an interpreter call out, "I am a man like you—do not be afraid!

sentences.zh: 會當使汝曹蘇息。

translations.literal: In time I shall surely let you all revive and rest.
translations.idiomatic: In time I will let you live and recover.

sentences.zh: 我無心南來，漢兵引我至此耳。」

translations.literal: I had no mind to come south—the Han troops drew me here, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I did not mean to march south; Han soldiers brought me here."

sentences.zh: 至明德門，下馬拜而後入宮。

translations.literal: Reaching the Gate of Illustrious Virtue, he dismounted, bowed, and then entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the Gate of Illustrious Virtue he dismounted, bowed, and only then entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 以其樞密副使劉密權開封尹事。

translations.literal: He appointed his Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Liu Mi to handle the duties of mayor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He put his vice commissioner of military affairs, Liu Mi, in charge of Kaifeng as acting mayor.

sentences.zh: 日暮，契丹主復出，屯於赤岡。

translations.literal: At day's end the Khitan emperor went out again and encamped at Chigang.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the Khitan emperor left the city again and camped at Red Mound.

sentences.zh: 戊子，執鄭州防禦使楊承勳至大梁，責以殺父叛契丹，命左右臠食之。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Yang Chengxun, defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, was seized and brought to Daliang. He was charged with killing his father and rebelling against the Khitan; the emperor ordered attendants to cut his flesh and eat it.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Yang Chengxun, military governor of Zheng, was brought to Daliang, accused of murdering his father and betraying the Khitan, and the emperor had his attendants carve up his flesh and devour it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以其弟右羽林將軍承信為平盧節度使，悉以其父舊兵授之。

translations.literal: Before long, his younger brother Chengxin, Right General of the Forest of Feathers, was made military governor of Pinglu, and all their father's former troops were given to him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his brother Chengxin, a general of the Right Forest of Feathers, was made governor of Pinglu and given all their father's old soldiers.

sentences.zh: 高勳訴張彥澤殺其家人於契丹主，契丹主亦怒彥澤剽掠京城，並傅住兒鎖之。

translations.literal: Gao Xun complained to the Khitan emperor that Zhang Yanzhe had killed his family. The Khitan emperor was also angry that Yanzhe had plundered the capital, and together with Fu Zhu'er had him put in chains.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xun accused Zhang Yanzhe before the Khitan emperor of slaughtering his household. The emperor was also furious that Yanzhe had looted the capital; he and Fu Zhu'er were shackled together.

sentences.zh: 以彥澤之罪宣示百官，問：「應死否？」

translations.literal: Yanzhe's crimes were proclaimed to the hundred officials, and they were asked: "Should he die?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhe's crimes were read out to the officials, who were asked, "Does he deserve death?"

sentences.zh: 皆言：「應死。」

translations.literal: All said: "He should die."
translations.idiomatic: All answered, "He should die."

sentences.zh: 百姓亦投牒爭疏彥澤罪。

translations.literal: The common people also submitted petitions competing to list Yanzhe's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners too flooded in with petitions detailing his offenses.

sentences.zh: 己丑，斬彥澤、住兒於北市，仍命高勳監刑。

translations.literal: On jichou, Yanzhe and Zhu'er were beheaded in the north market, and Gao Xun was still ordered to supervise the execution.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Yanzhe and Zhu'er were executed in the north market, with Gao Xun ordered to oversee the killing.

sentences.zh: 彥澤前所殺士大夫子孫，皆絰杖號哭，隨而詬詈，以杖撲之。

translations.literal: The sons and grandsons of scholar-officials whom Yanzhe had earlier killed all wore mourning headbands, leaned on staffs, and wailed; they followed along reviling him and beat him with their staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and grandsons of the scholar-officials he had murdered came in mourning, wailing and cursing, striking his corpse with their staffs.

sentences.zh: 勳命斷腕出鎖，剖其心以祭死者。

translations.literal: Xun ordered his wrist severed to remove the shackles, cut open his heart to sacrifice to the dead.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had his wrist cut free of the chains, opened his chest, and offered his heart to the dead.

sentences.zh: 市人爭破其腦取髓，臠其肉而食之。

translations.literal: Market people competed to smash his skull and take the marrow, cut his flesh into strips and eat it.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds in the market fought to crack his skull for marrow and slice his flesh to eat.

sentences.zh: 契丹送景延廣歸其國，庚寅，宿陳橋，夜，伺守者稍怠，扼吭而死。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent Jing Yanguang back to their country. On gengyin he lodged at Chen Bridge; in the night, watching until the guards slackened slightly, he throttled himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent Jing Yanguang homeward. On gengyin he stopped at Chen Bridge; in the night, when the guards relaxed, he seized his own throat and died.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，契丹以晉主為負義侯，置於黃龍府。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the Khitan made the Jin emperor Marquis Who Broke Faith and placed him in Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the Khitan demoted the Jin emperor to Marquis Who Broke Faith and sent him to Huanglong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 黃龍府，即慕容氏和龍城也。

translations.literal: Huanglong Prefecture is the same as the Murong clan's Helong City.
translations.idiomatic: Huanglong was the Murong capital Helong.

sentences.zh: 契丹主使謂李太后曰：「聞重貴不用母命以至於此，可求自便，勿與俱行。」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor sent someone to tell Empress Dowager Li: "I hear that Chonggui did not heed his mother's commands and came to this—she may seek her own convenience and need not travel with him."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor sent word to Empress Dowager Li: "I hear Chonggui ignored your counsel and brought ruin on himself. You may stay behind if you wish—do not travel with him."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「重貴事妾甚謹。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Chonggui served me with great care.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager replied, "Chonggui has always treated me with devotion.

sentences.zh: 所失者，違先君之志，絕兩國之歡耳。

translations.literal: Where he failed was in violating the former ruler's intent and severing the friendship between the two states, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: His fault was only to abandon our late lord's policy and break the peace between our realms.

sentences.zh: 今幸蒙大恩，全生保家，母不隨子，欲何所歸！」

translations.literal: Now, having fortunately received great grace to preserve life and household, if a mother does not follow her son, where would she go!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that we owe our lives to your mercy, where would a mother go if she did not follow her son?

sentences.zh: 癸巳，契丹遷晉主及其家人於封禪寺，遣大同節度使兼侍中河內崔廷勳以兵守之。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Khitan moved the Jin emperor and his family to Fengchan Temple and sent Cui Tingxun of Henei, military governor of Datong and concurrent palace attendant, with troops to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the Khitan moved the Jin emperor and his household to Fengchan Temple and posted Cui Tingxun of Henei—governor of Datong and palace attendant—with soldiers to guard them.

sentences.zh: 契丹主數遣使存問，晉主每聞使至，舉家憂恐。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor repeatedly sent envoys to inquire after them; whenever the Jin emperor heard an envoy had arrived, the whole household was anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor sent envoys again and again to inquire after them; each time one arrived, the whole household trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 時雨雪連旬，外無供億，上下凍餒。

translations.literal: At the time snow and rain continued for ten days; outside there were no supplies, and above and below they froze and starved.
translations.idiomatic: Snow and rain fell for ten days straight; no supplies reached them from outside, and everyone above and below went cold and hungry.

sentences.zh: 太后使人謂寺僧曰：「吾嘗於此飯僧數萬，今日獨無一人相念邪！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager sent someone to tell the temple monks: "I once fed tens of thousands of monks here—today is there truly not a single person who remembers me!"
translations.idiomatic: The dowager sent word to the monks: "I once fed tens of thousands of you here—has not one of you a thought for me now?"

sentences.zh: 僧辭以「虜意難測，不敢獻食。」

translations.literal: The monks declined on the grounds that "the barbarians' intentions are hard to fathom—we dare not offer food."
translations.idiomatic: The monks refused: "The invaders' intentions are unpredictable—we dare not bring food."

sentences.zh: 晉主陰祈守者，乃稍得食。

translations.literal: The Jin emperor secretly pleaded with the guards, and only then did they gradually obtain food.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor quietly begged the guards, and only then did they receive a little food.

sentences.zh: 是日，契丹主自赤岡引兵入宮，都城諸門及宮禁門，皆以契丹守衛，晝夜不釋兵仗。

translations.literal: That day the Khitan emperor led troops from Chigang into the palace. All gates of the capital and gates of the palace precinct were guarded by Khitan; day and night they did not lay down weapons.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Khitan emperor marched from Red Mound into the palace. Khitan soldiers held every city gate and palace gate, weapons in hand day and night.

sentences.zh: 磔犬於門，以竿懸羊皮於庭為厭勝。

translations.literal: They dismembered dogs at the gates and hung sheepskins on poles in the courtyard as apotropaic charms.
translations.idiomatic: Dogs were torn apart at the gates; sheepskins hung on poles in the courtyard as charms against evil.

sentences.zh: 契丹主謂晉群臣曰：「自今不修甲兵，不市戰馬，輕賦省役，天下太平矣。」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor said to the Jin ministers: "From now on, do not repair armor and weapons, do not buy war horses, lighten taxes and reduce corvée—the realm will be at peace."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor told the Jin ministers, "Henceforth cease repairing arms, cease buying war horses, lighten taxes and labor—and the realm will be at peace."

sentences.zh: 廢東京，降開封府為汴州，尹為防禦使。

translations.literal: He abolished the Eastern Capital, reduced Kaifeng Prefecture to Bian Prefecture, and made its mayor a defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the Eastern Capital, reduced Kaifeng to Bian Prefecture, and made its mayor a defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乙未，契丹主改服中國衣冠，百官起居皆如舊制。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Khitan emperor changed into Chinese cap and robes; the hundred officials' attendance ceremonies all followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the Khitan emperor donned Chinese dress; court ceremony resumed as before.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽、張礪共薦李崧之才。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou and Zhang Li together recommended Li Song's talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou and Zhang Li jointly praised Li Song's ability.

sentences.zh: 會威勝節度使馮道自鄧州入朝，契丹主素聞二人名，皆禮重之。

translations.literal: It happened that Feng Dao, military governor of Weisheng, entered court from Deng Prefecture. The Khitan emperor had long heard both men's names and honored them with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao, governor of Weisheng, arrived from Deng Prefecture to pay court. The Khitan emperor had long known both names and treated them with high honor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以崧為太子太師，充樞密使，道守太傅，於樞密院祗候，以備顧問。

translations.literal: Before long, Song was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and filled the post of commissioner of military affairs; Dao retained Grand Tutor and attended at the Bureau of Military Affairs to be available for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Song was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent and commissioner of military affairs; Dao remained grand tutor and waited at the bureau for consultation.

sentences.zh: 契丹主分遣使者，以詔書賜晉之籓鎮。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor separately dispatched envoys to bestow edicts on Jin's frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor sent envoys bearing edicts to Jin's military governors.

sentences.zh: 晉之籓鎮爭上表稱臣，被召者無不奔馳而至。

translations.literal: Jin's frontier commands competed to submit memorials declaring themselves subjects; none summoned failed to gallop and arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's governors rushed to submit pledges of allegiance; every man summoned raced to court.

sentences.zh: 惟彰義節度使史匡威據涇州不受命。

translations.literal: Only Zhangyi military governor Shi Kuangwei held Jing Prefecture and did not accept orders.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shi Kuangwei of Zhangyi held Jing Prefecture and refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 匡威，建瑭之子也。

translations.literal: Kuangwei was the son of Shi Jiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei was Jiantang's son.

sentences.zh: 雄武節度使何重建斬契丹使者，以秦、成、階三州降蜀。

translations.literal: Xiongwu military governor He Chongjian beheaded the Khitan envoy and surrendered the three prefectures Qin, Cheng, and Jie to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He Chongjian of Xiongwu killed the Khitan envoy and surrendered Qin, Cheng, and Jie to Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，杜重威既以晉軍降契丹，契丹主悉收其鎧仗數百萬貯恆州，驅馬數萬歸其國，遣重威將其眾從己而南。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Du Chongwei had surrendered the Jin army to the Khitan, the Khitan emperor collected all their armor and weapons—millions of pieces—and stored them at Heng Prefecture, drove tens of thousands of horses back to his country, and sent Chongwei to lead his troops south with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei surrendered the Jin army, the Khitan emperor seized millions of arms and armor for storage at Hengzhou, drove tens of thousands of horses north, and ordered Chongwei to march his men south with him.

sentences.zh: 及河，契丹主以晉兵之眾，恐其為變，欲悉以胡騎擁而納之河流。

translations.literal: When they reached the river, the Khitan emperor, because of the great number of Jin troops, feared they might mutiny and wished to have Khitan cavalry herd them all into the river.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yellow River, fearing mutiny from so many Jin soldiers, the Khitan emperor meant to have his horsemen drive them all into the water.

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「晉兵在他所者尚多，彼聞降者盡死，必皆拒命為患。

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated: "Jin troops elsewhere are still numerous; if they hear that all who surrendered were killed, they will surely all refuse orders and become a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: An adviser objected: "Many Jin troops remain elsewhere. If they hear every surrendering man was killed, they will resist—and become a plague.

sentences.zh: 不若且撫之，徐思其策。」

translations.literal: Better for now to soothe them and slowly consider a plan."
translations.idiomatic: Better pacify them now and plan more slowly."

sentences.zh: 契丹主乃使重威以其眾屯陳橋。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor then had Chongwei encamp his troops at Chen Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor then had Chongwei camp his men at Chen Bridge.

sentences.zh: 會久雪，官無所給，士卒凍餒，鹹怨重威，相聚而泣。

translations.literal: It happened that snow lasted long; the government provided nothing, and the soldiers froze and starved, all resenting Chongwei and gathering to weep.
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell for days; the state gave them nothing; the men froze and starved, cursed Chongwei, and wept together.

sentences.zh: 重威每出，道旁人皆罵之。

translations.literal: Whenever Chongwei went out, people along the road all cursed him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chongwei appeared in public, passersby cursed him.

sentences.zh: 契丹主猶欲誅晉兵。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor still wished to execute the Jin troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor still meant to slaughter the Jin soldiers.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽言於契丹主曰：「皇帝親冒矢石以取晉國，欲自有之乎，將為他人取之乎？」

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou said to the Khitan emperor: "Your Majesty personally braved arrows and stones to take the Jin state—do you wish to keep it for yourself, or have it taken for someone else?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou asked the Khitan emperor, "You braved battle to seize Jin—do you mean to keep it yourself, or let another take it?

sentences.zh: 契丹主變色曰：「朕舉國南征，五年不解甲，僅能得之，豈為他人乎！」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor changed color and said: "I mobilized the whole nation for the southern campaign, for five years did not ungird armor, and barely obtained it—how could it be for someone else!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flushed. "I marched the whole nation south, wore armor five years, and barely won it—how could it be for another!"

sentences.zh: 延壽曰：「晉國南有唐，西有蜀，常為仇敵，皇帝亦知之乎？」

translations.literal: Yanshou said: "South of Jin is Tang, west is Shu—they are constant foes. Does Your Majesty know this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou said, "Tang lies south of Jin, Shu west—they are your constant enemies. You know this?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「知之。」

translations.literal: He said: "I know."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I know."

sentences.zh: 延壽曰：「晉國東自沂、密，西及秦、鳳，延袤數千里，邊於吳、蜀，常以兵戍之。

translations.literal: Yanshou said: "Jin from the east at Yi and Mi west to Qin and Feng stretches several thousand li, bordering Wu and Shu, and must constantly be garrisoned with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou went on: "From Yi and Mi in the east to Qin and Feng in the west, Jin stretches thousands of li along Wu and Shu—troops must guard it always.

sentences.zh: 南方暑濕，上國之人不能居也。

translations.literal: The south is hot and humid; people of the northern state cannot dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: The south is hot and damp—your people cannot live there.

sentences.zh: 他日車駕北歸，以晉國如此之大，無兵守之，吳、蜀必相與乘虛入寇，如此，豈非為他人取之乎？」

translations.literal: Another day when the imperial carriage returns north, with Jin so vast and no troops to guard it, Wu and Shu will surely join to seize the opening and invade—would this not be having it taken for someone else?"
translations.idiomatic: When you ride north someday, who will hold so vast a realm? Wu and Shu will strike together—is that not giving Jin away?"

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「我不知也。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor said: "I did not know.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I had not thought of that.

sentences.zh: 然則奈何？」

translations.literal: Then what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: What should we do?"

sentences.zh: 延壽曰：「陳橋降卒，可分以戍南邊，則吳、蜀不能為患矣。」

translations.literal: Yanshou said: "The surrendered troops at Chen Bridge can be divided to garrison the southern border—then Wu and Shu cannot become a scourge."
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou said, "Divide the Chen Bridge surrenderers to guard the south, and Wu and Shu will not trouble you."

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「吾昔在上黨，失於斷割，悉以唐兵授晉。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor said: "Long ago at Shangdang I failed in decisive cutting off and gave all Tang troops to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "At Shangdang I failed to finish the job and handed Tang's army to Jin.

sentences.zh: 既而返為仇讎，北向與吾戰，辛勤累年，僅能勝之。

translations.literal: They then turned back into foes, faced north to fight me, and through years of toil I barely could overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: They became my enemies, fought me for years, and I barely beat them.

sentences.zh: 今幸入吾手，不因此時悉除之，豈可復留以為後患乎？」

translations.literal: Now, having fortunately come into my hand, if I do not at this time eliminate them all, how could I leave them again to become a later scourge?"
translations.idiomatic: Now they are in my grasp—if I do not destroy them now, how can I leave a future threat?

sentences.zh: 延壽曰：「曏留晉兵於河南，不質其妻子，故有此憂。

translations.literal: Yanshou said: "Formerly Jin troops were left south of the river without taking their wives and children as hostages—hence this worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou said, "Last time you left Jin troops south of the river without holding their families hostage—that is why you worry.

sentences.zh: 今若悉徙其家於恆、定、雲、朔之間，每歲分番使戍南邊，何憂其為變哉！

translations.literal: Now if all their families are moved between Heng, Ding, Yun, and Shuo, and each year they rotate in turns to garrison the southern border, what worry is there that they will mutiny!
translations.idiomatic: Move every family to Heng, Ding, Yun, and Shuo, rotate them south by turns each year—what fear of mutiny then! That is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 此上策也。」

translations.literal: This is the superior stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: That is the best course.

sentences.zh: 契丹主悅曰：「善！

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor said with pleasure: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor was pleased. "Good!

sentences.zh: 惟大王所以處之。」

translations.literal: Let the great king handle it as he sees fit."
translations.idiomatic: Great King, handle it as you will."

sentences.zh: 由是陳橋兵始得免，分遣還營。

translations.literal: From this the Chen Bridge troops were first spared and sent back to camp in divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Chen Bridge men were spared and sent back to their camps.

sentences.zh: 契丹主殺右金吾衛大將軍李彥紳、宦者秦繼旻，以其為唐潞王殺東丹王故也。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor killed Right Golden Crow Guard General Li Yanshen and eunuch Qin Jimin because they had killed the Eastern Dān king on behalf of Tang's Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor executed Li Yanshen of the Right Golden Crow Guard and the eunuch Qin Jimin for their part in the Tang Prince of Lu's murder of the Eastern Dān prince.

sentences.zh: 以其家族貲財賜東丹王之子永康王兀欲。

translations.literal: Their families' property and wealth were bestowed on the Eastern Dān king's son, Prince of Yongkang Wuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Their families' goods were given to the Eastern Dān prince's son, Prince Yongkang Wuyu.

sentences.zh: 兀欲眇一目，為人雄健好施。

translations.literal: Wuyu was blind in one eye; as a man he was bold and strong and fond of giving.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu was blind in one eye, a bold and generous man.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，晉主與李太后、安太妃、馮后及弟睿、子延煦、延寶俱北遷，後宮左右從者百餘人。

translations.literal: On guimao, the Jin emperor with Empress Dowager Li, Consort Tai An, Empress Feng, and his younger brother Rui, sons Yanshu and Yanbao, all moved north; from the inner palace and attendants left and right, more than a hundred followed.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Jin emperor, Empress Dowager Li, Consort Tai An, Empress Feng, his brother Rui, and sons Yanshu and Yanbao marched north with more than a hundred palace women and attendants.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣三百騎援送之，又遣晉中書令趙瑩、樞密使馮玉、馬軍都指揮使李彥韜與之俱。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent three hundred horsemen to escort them, and also sent Jin's Secretariat Director Zhao Ying, Commissioner of Military Affairs Feng Yu, and Horse Army Commander-in-Chief Li Yantao to go with them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent three hundred horsemen as escort, and ordered Zhao Ying, Feng Yu, and Li Yantao of Jin to accompany them.

sentences.zh: 晉主在塗，供饋不繼，或時與太后俱絕食，舊臣無敢進謁者。

translations.literal: The Jin emperor on the road had supplies that did not continue; sometimes he and the empress dowager together had no food; former ministers dared not come forward to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: On the road supplies failed; sometimes he and the dowager went without food; no former minister dared visit.

sentences.zh: 獨磁州刺史李穀迎謁於路，相對泣下。

translations.literal: Only Cizhou prefect Li Gu met them on the road to pay respects; facing each other they wept.
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Gu, prefect of Cizhou, met them on the road and wept face to face.

sentences.zh: 穀曰：「臣無狀，負陛下。」

translations.literal: Gu said: "Your servant is without proper form and has failed Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "I am unworthy—I have failed Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 因傾貲以獻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he poured out his wealth as an offering.
translations.idiomatic: He poured out his wealth as a gift.

sentences.zh: 晉主至中度橋，見杜重威寨，歎曰：「天乎！

translations.literal: When the Jin emperor reached Zhongdu Bridge and saw Du Chongwei's camp, he sighed: "Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongdu Bridge the Jin emperor saw Du Chongwei's camp and cried, "Heaven!

sentences.zh: 我家何負，為此賊所破！」

translations.literal: What did my house do wrong, to be ruined by this traitor!"
translations.idiomatic: What did my house do to deserve ruin by this traitor!"

sentences.zh: 慟哭而去。

translations.literal: He wailed and went on.
translations.idiomatic: He wept bitterly and passed on.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，蜀主以左千牛衛上將軍李繼勳為秦州宣慰使。

translations.literal: On guichou, the Shu ruler appointed Left Thousand-Ox Guard General Li Jixun as commissioner to console Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou the Shu emperor named Li Jixun of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard commissioner to console Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 契丹主以前燕京留守劉晞為西京留守，永康王兀欲之弟留珪為義成節度使，族人郎五為鎮寧節度使，兀欲姊婿潘聿撚為橫海節度使，趙延壽之子匡贊為護國節度使，漢將張彥超為雄武節度使，史佺為彰義節度使，客省副使劉晏僧為忠武節度使，前護國節度使侯益為鳳翔節度使，權知鳳翔府事焦繼勳為保大節度使。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor made former Yanjing garrison commander Liu Xi western capital garrison commander; Prince of Yongkang Wuyu's younger brother Liugui military governor of Yicheng; clansman Langwu military governor of Zhenning; Wuyu's sister's husband Pan Yuzhen military governor of Henghai; Zhao Yanshou's son Kuangzan military governor of Huguo; Han general Zhang Yanchao military governor of Xiongwu; Shi Quan military governor of Zhangyi; Vice Commissioner of the Reception Bureau Liu Yanseng military governor of Zhongwu; former Huguo military governor Hou Yi military governor of Fengxiang; acting Fengxiang prefect Jiao Jixun military governor of Baoda.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor appointed Liu Xi, former Yanjing commander, western capital commander; Wuyu's brother Liugui governor of Yicheng; clansman Langwu of Zhenning; Wuyu's brother-in-law Pan Yuzhen of Henghai; Yanshou's son Kuangzan of Huguo; Han general Zhang Yanchao of Xiongwu; Shi Quan of Zhangyi; reception vice commissioner Liu Yanseng of Zhongwu; former Huguo governor Hou Yi of Fengxiang; and acting Fengxiang prefect Jiao Jixun of Baoda.

sentences.zh: 晞，涿州人也。

translations.literal: Xi was a man of Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was from Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而何重建附蜀，史匡威不受代，契丹勢稍沮。

translations.literal: Before long He Chongjian attached himself to Shu, Shi Kuangwei did not accept replacement, and Khitan momentum was slightly checked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon He Chongjian went over to Shu, Shi Kuangwei refused transfer, and Khitan momentum faltered.

sentences.zh: 晉昌節度使趙在禮入朝，其裨將留長安者作亂，節度副使建人李肅討誅之，軍府以安。

translations.literal: Jinchang military governor Zhao Zaili entered court; his lieutenant generals left at Chang'an mutinied; vice military governor Li Su of Jian Prefecture attacked and executed them, and the army headquarters was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili of Jinchang came to court; subordinates left at Chang'an mutinied; vice governor Li Su of Jian suppressed them, and the command was pacified.

sentences.zh: 晉主之絕契丹也，匡國節度使劉繼勳為宣徽北院使，頗預其謀。

translations.literal: When the Jin emperor broke with the Khitan, Kuangguo military governor Liu Jixun was northern commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and took part considerably in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin emperor broke with the Khitan, Liu Jixun of Kuangguo, northern palace commissioner, had helped plan it.

sentences.zh: 契丹主入汴，繼勳入朝，契丹主責之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan emperor entered Bian, Jixun entered court and the Khitan emperor reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor entered Bian, Jixun presented himself and was rebuked.

sentences.zh: 時馮道在殿上，繼勳急指道曰：「馮道為首相，與景延廣實為此謀。

translations.literal: At the time Feng Dao was in the hall; Jixun hastily pointed at Dao and said: "Feng Dao as chief minister, together with Jing Yanguang, truly made this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao stood in the hall; Jixun pointed at him and said, "Chief Minister Feng Dao and Jing Yanguang truly devised this plot.

sentences.zh: 臣位卑，何敢發言！」

translations.literal: Your servant's position is low—how would I dare to speak!"
translations.idiomatic: I am too low in rank to speak!

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「此叟非多事者，勿妄引之！」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor said: "This old fellow is not a meddler—do not falsely implicate him!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor said, "This old man is no troublemaker—do not drag him in falsely!"

sentences.zh: 命鎖繼勳，將送黃龍府。

translations.literal: He ordered Jixun shackled and to be sent to Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jixun shackled for transport to Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮至洛陽，謂人曰：「契丹主嘗言莊宗之亂由我所致。

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili reached Luoyang and said to people: "The Khitan emperor once said that the turmoil of Emperor Zhuangzong was caused by me.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zaili reached Luoyang he told others, "The Khitan emperor once said Zhuangzong's turmoil was my doing.

sentences.zh: 我此行良可憂。」

translations.literal: This journey of mine is truly cause for worry."
translations.idiomatic: This trip of mine is deeply worrying."

sentences.zh: 契丹主遣契丹將述軋、奚王拽刺、勃海將高謨翰戍洛陽，在禮入謁，拜於庭下，拽刺等皆踞坐受之。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor sent Khitan general Shuzha, Xi king Zhuaici, and Bohai general Gao Mohan to garrison Luoyang. Zaili entered to pay respects and bowed in the courtyard; Zhuaici and the others all sat with legs sprawled to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor posted Shuzha, Xi king Zhuaici, and Bohai general Gao Mohan at Luoyang. Zaili came to court and bowed in the courtyard; Zhuaici and the others received him sprawled on their seats.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，在禮至鄭州，聞繼勳被鎖，大驚，夜，自經於馬櫪間。

translations.literal: On yimao, Zaili reached Zheng Prefecture; hearing Jixun had been shackled, he was greatly alarmed, and in the night hanged himself in the horse stable.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Zaili reached Zhengzhou; learning Jixun was shackled, he was terrified and hanged himself that night in the stable.

sentences.zh: 契丹主聞在禮死，乃釋繼勳，繼勳憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: When the Khitan emperor heard Zaili was dead, he then released Jixun; Jixun died from grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Zaili's death, the Khitan emperor released Jixun, who died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 劉晞在契丹嘗為樞密使、同平章事，至洛陽，詬奚王曰：「趙在禮漢家大臣，爾北方一酋長耳，安得慢之如此！」

translations.literal: Liu Xi in the Khitan state had once been commissioner of military affairs and concurrent Grand Councilor. Reaching Luoyang, he reviled the Xi king: "Zhao Zaili is a Han dynasty minister—you are merely a northern chieftain—how dare you treat him with such contempt!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xi, once Khitan commissioner of military affairs and grand councilor, reached Luoyang and berated the Xi king: "Zhao Zaili is a Han minister—you are only a northern chieftain—how dare you insult him so!"

sentences.zh: 立於庭下以挫之。

translations.literal: He stood in the courtyard below to humble them.
translations.idiomatic: He stood in the courtyard to put them in their place.

sentences.zh: 由是洛人稍安。

translations.literal: From this the people of Luoyang were somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: After that the people of Luoyang felt somewhat safer.

sentences.zh: 契丹主廣受四方貢獻，大縱酒作樂，每謂晉臣曰：「中國事，我皆知之；

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor broadly received tribute from the four directions and indulged greatly in wine and music. He often said to Jin ministers: "Matters of China—I know them all;
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor took tribute from every quarter and feasted endlessly. He often told Jin ministers, "I know all affairs of China;

sentences.zh: 吾國事，汝曹弗知也。」

translations.literal: matters of our state—you do not know."
translations.idiomatic: but you know nothing of our state's affairs."

sentences.zh: 趙延壽請給上國兵廩食，契丹主曰：「吾國無此法。」

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou requested grain rations for the northern state's troops. The Khitan emperor said: "Our state has no such practice."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou asked for grain rations for Khitan troops. The Khitan emperor said, "We have no such custom.

sentences.zh: 乃縱胡騎四出，以牧馬為名，分番剽掠，謂之「打草穀」。

translations.literal: He then let Khitan cavalry ride out in the four directions, under the name of grazing horses, taking turns to plunder—this was called "beating the grass for grain."
translations.idiomatic: Instead he sent Khitan horsemen in every direction under the pretense of grazing horses, rotating bands to loot—called "beating the grass for grain."

sentences.zh: 丁壯斃於鋒刃，老弱委以溝壑，自東、西南畿及鄭、滑、曹、濮，數百里間，財畜殆盡。

translations.literal: Strong men fell to blades; old and weak were cast into ditches and ravines. From the eastern and western capital districts to Zheng, Hua, Cao, and Pu, for several hundred li, wealth and livestock were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Able men died by the sword; the old and weak were left in ditches. From the capital districts east and west through Zheng, Hua, Cao, and Pu, for hundreds of li, property and livestock were stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 契丹主謂判三司劉昫曰：「契丹兵三十萬，既平晉國，應有優賜，速宜營辦。」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor said to Director of the Three Offices Liu Xu: "Three hundred thousand Khitan troops, having pacified the Jin state, ought to receive generous rewards—hasten to arrange it."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor told Liu Xu, director of the three offices, "Three hundred thousand Khitan soldiers have conquered Jin and deserve rich rewards—prepare them at once."

sentences.zh: 時府庫空竭，昫不知所出，請括借都城士民錢帛，自將相以下皆不免。

translations.literal: At the time the treasuries were empty and exhausted; Xu did not know where to obtain funds and requested forced loans of money and silk from the capital's gentry and commoners—from chancellors and generals downward none were exempt.
translations.idiomatic: The treasuries were empty. Xu knew no source and proposed forced loans from the capital's people—from ministers and generals down, no one was spared.

sentences.zh: 又分遣使者數十人詣諸州括借，皆迫以嚴誅，人不聊生。

translations.literal: He also separately sent several dozen envoys to the various prefectures for forced loans, all compelled by threat of severe execution; people could not sustain life.
translations.idiomatic: He sent dozens of envoys to every prefecture to levy loans under threat of death; the people could not live.

sentences.zh: 其實無所頒給，皆蓄之內庫，欲輦歸其國。

translations.literal: In truth nothing was distributed; all was stored in the inner treasury, intending to cart it back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In fact nothing was distributed; everything went to the inner treasury to be carted north.

sentences.zh: 於是內外怨憤，始患苦契丹，皆思逐之矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon inside and outside were resentful and furious; they first suffered under the Khitan and all thought of driving them out.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside alike turned bitter; people first felt the Khitan as a plague and all began to dream of expelling them.

sentences.zh: 初，晉主與河東節度使、中書令、北平王劉知遠相猜忌，雖以為北面行營都統，徒尊以虛名，而諸軍進止，實不得預聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jin emperor and Hedong military governor, Secretariat Director, and Prince of Beiping Liu Zhiyuan were mutually suspicious. Although he was made overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters, it was only an empty honor in name, and in truth he could not be informed of the armies' advances and halts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jin emperor and Liu Zhiyuan of Hedong—secretariat director and Prince of Beiping—mistrusted each other. Though named overall commander of the northern armies, it was an empty title; he was never told when troops marched or halted.

sentences.zh: 知遠因之廣募士卒。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan thereupon broadly recruited soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan used the interval to recruit widely.

sentences.zh: 陽城之戰，諸軍散卒歸之者數千人，又得吐谷渾財畜，由是河東富強冠諸鎮，步騎至五萬人。

translations.literal: From the battle at Yangcheng, scattered troops of the various armies who returned to him numbered several thousand; he also obtained Tuyuhun wealth and livestock. From this Hedong's wealth and strength topped all commands, with infantry and cavalry reaching fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After Yangcheng, thousands of scattered soldiers rallied to him; Tuyuhun wealth and herds followed. Hedong became the richest command, with fifty thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 晉主與契丹結怨，知遠知其必危，而未嘗論諫。

translations.literal: When the Jin emperor bore a grudge with the Khitan, Zhiyuan knew he would surely be in peril, yet never remonstrated or advised.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin emperor broke with the Khitan, Zhiyuan knew disaster was coming but never spoke against it.

sentences.zh: 契丹屢深入，知遠初無邀遮、入援之志。

translations.literal: As the Khitan repeatedly penetrated deep, at first Zhiyuan had no intent to intercept or send relief.
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitan raided deep, Zhiyuan at first showed no will to block them or send aid.

sentences.zh: 及聞契丹入汴，知遠分兵守四境以防侵軼。

translations.literal: When he heard the Khitan had entered Bian, Zhiyuan divided troops to guard the four borders against raids.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the Khitan had entered Bian, he posted troops on every border against incursion.

sentences.zh: 遣客將安陽王峻奉三表詣契丹主：一，賀入汴；

translations.literal: He sent guest general Wang Jun of Anyang to present three memorials to the Khitan emperor: first, to congratulate entering Bian;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Jun of Anyang with three memorials to the Khitan emperor: first, congratulations on entering Bian;

sentences.zh: 二，以太原夷、夏雜居，戍兵所聚，未敢離鎮；

translations.literal: second, that Taiyuan has Yi and Xia mixed together and garrison troops gathered, so he dared not leave his post;
translations.idiomatic: second, that Taiyuan mixes barbarian and Chinese and holds many garrisons, so he dared not leave his post;

sentences.zh: 三，以應有貢物，值契丹將劉九一軍自土門西入屯於南川，城中憂懼，俟召還此軍，道路始通，可以入貢。

translations.literal: third, that tribute goods were due, but it happened that Khitan general Liu Jiuyi's army entered from Tumen Pass westward and encamped at Nanchuan; the city was anxious and afraid—when this army is recalled, the roads will be open and tribute can be presented.
translations.idiomatic: third, that tribute was due but General Liu Jiuyi's Khitan force had entered from Tumen and camped at Nanchuan, frightening the city—once that army was recalled and roads cleared, tribute could be sent.

sentences.zh: 契丹主賜詔褒美，及進書，親加「兒」字於知遠姓名之上，仍賜以木柺。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor bestowed an edict praising him, and on the submitted letter personally added the character "son" above Zhiyuan's name, still bestowing a wooden staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor sent a commendatory edict, wrote the character for "son" above Zhiyuan's name on his letter, and gave him a wooden staff.

sentences.zh: 胡法，優禮大臣則賜之，如漢賜幾仗之比，惟偉王以叔父之尊得之。

translations.literal: By Khitan law, to honor a great minister they bestow it, comparable to Han bestowal of armrest and staff—only the Prince of Wei, by his uncle's exalted rank, had received it.
translations.idiomatic: By Khitan custom such a staff honored great ministers, as Han armrests and staffs did—only the Prince of Wei, as the emperor's uncle, had received one before.

sentences.zh: 知遠又遣北都副留守太原白文珂入獻奇繒名馬，契丹主知知遠觀望不至，及文珂還，使謂知遠曰：「汝不事南朝，又不事北朝，意欲何所俟邪？」

translations.literal: Zhiyuan also sent northern capital vice garrison commander Bai Wenke of Taiyuan to present rare silks and famous horses. The Khitan emperor knew Zhiyuan was watching and waiting and did not come; when Wenke returned, he sent word to Zhiyuan: "You do not serve the southern court, nor do you serve the northern court—what are you waiting for?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan also sent Bai Wenke of Taiyuan with rare silks and fine horses. Knowing Zhiyuan was holding back, when Wenke returned the Khitan emperor asked Zhiyuan, "You serve neither south nor north—what are you waiting for?"

sentences.zh: 蕃漢孔目官郭威言於知遠曰：「虜恨我深矣！

translations.literal: The Khitan-Han clerk Guo Wei said to Zhiyuan: "The barbarians hate us deeply!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei, his Khitan-Han clerk, told Zhiyuan, "The barbarians hate us deeply!

sentences.zh: 王峻言契丹貪殘失人心，必不能久有中國。」

translations.literal: Wang Jun says the Khitan are greedy and cruel and have lost people's hearts—they surely cannot long hold China."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun says the Khitan are greedy and cruel, have lost the people's hearts, and cannot long hold China."

sentences.zh: 或勸知遠舉兵進取。

translations.literal: Some urged Zhiyuan to raise troops and seize the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Zhiyuan to march and seize power.

sentences.zh: 知遠曰：「用兵有緩有急，當隨時制宜。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan said: "Using troops has its slow and its urgent—one must suit the times.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan said, "War has its seasons—one must suit the moment.

sentences.zh: 今契丹新降晉軍十萬，虎據京邑，未有他變，豈可輕動哉！

translations.literal: Now the Khitan have newly accepted a hundred thousand surrendered Jin troops, crouching like tigers over the capital—no other change has occurred—how could one move lightly!
translations.idiomatic: Now a hundred thousand surrendered Jin troops bolster them in the capital—nothing else has shifted—how can we move rashly!

sentences.zh: 且觀其所利止於貨財，貨財既足，必將北去。

translations.literal: Moreover, observe that what they seek stops at goods and wealth; once goods and wealth are enough, they will surely go north.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, they care only for loot; once they have enough, they will go north.

sentences.zh: 況冰雪已消，勢難久留，宜待其去，然後取之，可以萬全。」

translations.literal: Moreover the ice and snow have already melted—it will be hard for their momentum to stay long. Better to wait until they leave, then take it—this can be ten thousand times secure."
translations.idiomatic: The ice has melted—they cannot stay long. Wait until they leave, then take it—that is the sure course."

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使張從恩，以地迫懷、洛，欲入朝於契丹，遣使謀於知遠。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi military governor Zhang Cong'en, because his territory pressed on Huai and Luo, wished to enter court before the Khitan and sent an envoy to consult Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong'en of Zhaoyi, pressed by Huai and Luo, wished to pay court to the Khitan and sent an envoy to consult Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 知遠曰：「我以一隅之地，安敢抗天下之大！

translations.literal: Zhiyuan said: "With my corner of territory, how would I dare resist the greatness of all under heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan said, "With my little corner, how dare I resist the realm!

sentences.zh: 君宜先行，我當繼往。」

translations.literal: My lord should go first; I shall follow after."
translations.idiomatic: You should go first; I will follow."

sentences.zh: 從恩以為然。

translations.literal: Cong'en thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: Cong'en agreed.

sentences.zh: 判官高防諫曰：「公晉室懿親，不可輕變臣節。」

translations.literal: Judge Gao Fang remonstrated: "Your Excellency is a close kin of the Jin house—you must not lightly change your subject's loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: His judge Gao Fang objected: "You are close kin to the Jin house—you must not lightly abandon your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 從恩不從。

translations.literal: Cong'en did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Cong'en would not listen.

sentences.zh: 左驍衛大將軍王守恩，與從恩姻家，時在上黨，從恩以副使趙行遷知留後，牒守恩權巡檢使，與高防佐之，遂行。

translations.literal: Left Martial Guard General Wang Shou'en, related to Cong'en by marriage, was then at Shangdang. Cong'en made vice commissioner Zhao Xingqian acting garrison commander, issued a dispatch making Shou'en acting inspection commissioner to assist Fang with Gao Fang, and then set out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shou'en of the Left Martial Guard, Cong'en's in-law, was at Shangdang. Cong'en left Zhao Xingqian as acting commander, made Shou'en acting inspector with Gao Fang to assist, and departed.

sentences.zh: 守恩，建立之子也。

translations.literal: Shou'en was the son of Wang Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: Shou'en was Jianli's son.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使高從誨遣使入貢於契丹，契丹遣使以馬賜之。

translations.literal: Jingnan military governor Gao Conghui sent envoys to present tribute to the Khitan; the Khitan sent envoys to bestow horses on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Conghui of Jingnan sent tribute to the Khitan; the Khitan sent horses in return.

sentences.zh: 從誨亦遣使詣河東勸進。

translations.literal: Conghui also sent envoys to Hedong to urge assumption of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Conghui also sent envoys to Hedong urging Zhiyuan to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 唐主立齊王景遂為皇太弟。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler established Prince of Qi Jing Sui as imperial younger brother heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor named Prince of Qi Jing Sui imperial younger brother heir.

sentences.zh: 徙燕王景達為齊王，領諸道兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: He moved Prince of Yan Jing Da to Prince of Qi and made him commander-in-chief of armies and horses of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He moved Prince of Yan Jing Da to Prince of Qi and made him commander-in-chief of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 徙南昌王弘冀為燕王，為之副。

translations.literal: He moved Prince of Nanchang Hong Ji to Prince of Yan as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He moved Prince of Nanchang Hong Ji to Prince of Yan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 景遂嘗與宮僚燕集，贊善大夫元城張易有所規諫，景遂方與客傳玩玉懷，弗之顧，易怒曰：「殿下重寶而輕士。」

translations.literal: Jing Sui once banqueted with palace staff; Remonstrating Grandee Zhang Yi of Yuancheng offered admonition. Jing Sui was just passing around a jade cup with guests and did not heed him, easily angered, saying: "Your Highness values treasure and treats scholars lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Sui once feasted with palace staff. Zhang Yi of Yuancheng remonstrated while Jing Sui passed a jade cup among guests and ignored him. Yi snapped, "Your Highness treasures gems and slight scholars.

sentences.zh: 取杯抵地碎之，眾皆失色。

translations.literal: He took the cup and struck the ground, shattering it; the assembly all lost color.
translations.idiomatic: He dashed the cup to the floor and shattered it; everyone blanched.

sentences.zh: 景遂斂容謝之，待易益厚。

translations.literal: Jing Sui composed his expression and apologized to him, treating Yi all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Sui composed himself and apologized, treating Yi with even greater respect.

sentences.zh: 景達性剛直，唐主與宗室近臣飲，馮延己、延魯、魏岑、陳覺輩，極傾諂之態，或乘酒喧笑。

translations.literal: Jing Da's nature was firm and upright. When the Tang ruler drank with close kin of the imperial clan, Feng Yanji, Yanlu, Wei Qin, Chen Jue, and their sort displayed extreme fawning, sometimes taking advantage of wine to clamor and laugh.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Da was blunt by nature. When the Tang emperor drank with kin and close ministers, Feng Yanji, Yanlu, Wei Qin, Chen Jue, and their circle fawned extravagantly and sometimes shouted with drink.

sentences.zh: 景達屢訶責之，復極言諫唐主，以不宜親近佞臣。

translations.literal: Jing Da repeatedly rebuked and reproached them, and again spoke bluntly to remonstrate with the Tang ruler that he should not be close to flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Da repeatedly scolded them and bluntly warned the Tang emperor not to keep flatterers close.

sentences.zh: 延己以二弟立非己意，欲以虛言德之。

translations.literal: Yanji, because his two younger brothers' establishment was not his intent, wished to win them with empty praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yanji, unhappy that his two younger brothers had been elevated, tried to win them with empty praise.

sentences.zh: 嘗宴東宮，陽醉，撫景達背曰：「爾不可忘我！」

translations.literal: Once at a banquet in the Eastern Palace he feigned drunkenness, stroked Jing Da's back and said: "You must not forget me!"
translations.idiomatic: At an Eastern Palace feast he pretended drunkenness, patted Jing Da's back, and said, "You must not forget me!

sentences.zh: 景達大怒，拂衣入禁中白唐主，請斬之。

translations.literal: Jing Da was greatly angered, shook out his robes, entered the inner palace to inform the Tang ruler, and requested he be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Da flew into a rage, strode into the inner palace, and asked the Tang emperor to execute him.

sentences.zh: 唐主諭解，乃止。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler admonished and reconciled him, and only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor calmed him and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 張易謂景達曰：「群小交構，禍福所繫。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi said to Jing Da: "Petty men weave plots—fortune and disaster hang on this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi told Jing Da, "Petty men weave plots—your fortune hangs on how you treat them.

sentences.zh: 殿下力未能去，數面折之，使彼懼而為備，何所不至！」

translations.literal: Your Highness's strength is not yet enough to remove them; repeatedly to shame them to their faces makes them afraid and take precautions—what would not they dare!"
translations.idiomatic: You are not strong enough to remove them yet; shaming them to their faces only makes them fear you and prepare—what might they not do!

sentences.zh: 自是每游宴，景達多辭疾不預。

translations.literal: From this, whenever there were outings and banquets, Jing Da mostly declined on grounds of illness and did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: After that Jing Da usually pleaded illness and skipped banquets.

sentences.zh: 唐主遣使賀契丹滅晉，且請詣長安修復唐室諸陵。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler sent envoys to congratulate the Khitan on destroying Jin, and also requested to go to Chang'an to repair the various tombs of the Tang house.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor sent envoys to congratulate the Khitan on destroying Jin and asked permission to restore the Tang imperial tombs at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 契丹不許，而遣使報之。

translations.literal: The Khitan did not permit it but sent envoys to reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan refused but sent envoys in reply.

sentences.zh: 晉密州刺史皇甫暉，棣州刺史王建，皆避契丹，帥眾奔唐。

translations.literal: Jin's Mizhou prefect Huangfu Hui and Dizhou prefect Wang Jian both fled the Khitan and led their troops to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui of Mizhou and Wang Jian of Dizhou, fleeing the Khitan, led their men to Tang.

sentences.zh: 淮北賊帥多請命於唐。

translations.literal: Bandit chiefs north of the Huai mostly requested orders from Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit leaders north of the Huai mostly submitted to Tang.

sentences.zh: 唐虞部員外郎史館修撰韓熙載上疏，以為：「陛下恢復祖業，今也其時。

translations.literal: Tang's Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Historiography Compiler Han Xizai submitted a memorial, holding that: "Your Majesty's restoration of the ancestral enterprise—now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xizai, Tang vice director of rites and historiographer, memorialized: "Your Majesty can restore the ancestral enterprise—now is the time.

sentences.zh: 若虜主北歸，中原有主，則未易圖也。」

translations.literal: If the barbarian ruler returns north and the central plains have a master, then it will not be easy to plan."
translations.idiomatic: If the Khitan emperor goes north and the central plains find a ruler, the chance will be gone."

sentences.zh: 時方連兵福州，未暇北顧。

translations.literal: At the time they were just then linking troops at Fuzhou and had no leisure to look north.
translations.idiomatic: But Tang was tied up campaigning at Fuzhou and could not look north.

sentences.zh: 唐人皆以為恨，唐主亦悔之。

translations.literal: Tang people all regarded it as a regret; the Tang ruler also regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Tang subjects mourned the missed chance; the Tang emperor regretted it too.

sentences.zh: 契丹主召晉百官悉集於庭，問曰：「吾國廣大，方數萬里，有君長二十七人。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor summoned all Jin's hundred officials to assemble in the courtyard and asked: "Our state is vast, several tens of thousands of li square, with twenty-seven rulers.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor summoned all Jin officials to the courtyard and asked, "Our realm spans tens of thousands of li with twenty-seven rulers.

sentences.zh: 今中國之俗異於吾國，吾欲擇一人君之，如何？」

translations.literal: Now China's customs differ from our state's—I wish to choose one person to rule it—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: China's customs differ from ours—I wish to choose someone to rule it—what say you?

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「天無二日。

translations.literal: All said: "Heaven has no two suns.
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Heaven has but one sun.

sentences.zh: 夷、夏之心，皆願推戴皇帝。」

translations.literal: Barbarian and Chinese hearts alike all wish to elevate and support Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian and Chinese alike wish to acclaim Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 如是者再。

translations.literal: Thus it was twice.
translations.idiomatic: They said so twice.

sentences.zh: 契丹主乃曰：「汝曹既欲君我，今茲所行，何事為先？」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor then said: "Since you all wish me as ruler, in what you do now, what matter should come first?"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor then said, "Since you wish me as ruler, what should come first?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「王者初有天下，應大赦。」

translations.literal: They replied: "When a king first possesses all under heaven, he should grant a great amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "A new ruler should proclaim a great amnesty."

sentences.zh: 二月，丁巳朔，契丹主服通天冠、絳紗袍，登正殿，設樂懸、儀衛於庭。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day of the month dingsi, the Khitan emperor wore the penetrating-heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, ascended the main hall, and set musical bells and ceremonial guards in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day dingsi, the Khitan emperor wore the penetrating-heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, entered the main hall, and set bells and guards in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 百官朝賀，華人皆法服，胡人仍胡服，立於文武班中間。

translations.literal: The hundred officials paid court congratulations; Chinese all wore court dress, Khitan still wore Khitan dress, standing between the civil and military ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Officials paid homage; Chinese wore court dress, Khitan kept Khitan dress, standing between the civil and military ranks.

sentences.zh: 下制稱大遼會同十年，大赦。

translations.literal: An edict was issued proclaiming Great Liao, year ten of Huitong, with a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed Great Liao, year ten of Huitong, with a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 仍云：「自今節度使、刺史，毋得置牙兵，市戰馬。」

translations.literal: It still said: "From now on military governors and prefects must not establish guard troops or buy war horses."
translations.idiomatic: It also decreed that henceforth governors and prefects must not keep guard troops or buy war horses."

sentences.zh: 趙延壽以契丹主負約，心怏怏，令李崧言於契丹主曰：「漢天子所不敢望，乞為皇太子。」

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou, because the Khitan emperor had broken his promise, was resentful in heart and had Li Song speak to the Khitan emperor: "What a Han Son of Heaven would not dare hope for—I beg to be made crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou, angry that the Khitan emperor had broken his word, had Li Song ask to be made crown prince—more than any Han emperor would dare request.

sentences.zh: 崧不得已為言之。

translations.literal: Song had no choice but to speak it for him.
translations.idiomatic: Song had no choice but to relay the request.

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「我於燕王，雖割吾肉，有用於燕王，吾無所愛。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor said: "Toward the Prince of Yan—even if I cut my own flesh, if it is useful to the Prince of Yan, I love nothing I would not give.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor said, "For the Prince of Yan I would cut my own flesh if it served him—I withhold nothing.

sentences.zh: 然吾聞皇太子當以天子兒為之，豈燕王所可為也！」

translations.literal: Yet I have heard the crown prince ought to be made from the Son of Heaven's son—how could the Prince of Yan do it!"
translations.idiomatic: But I hear the crown prince must be the emperor's own son—how could the Prince of Yan qualify!

sentences.zh: 因令為燕王遷官。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered offices transferred for the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered new offices for the Prince of Yan instead.

sentences.zh: 時契丹以恆州為中京，翰林承旨張礪奏擬燕王中京留守、大丞相、錄尚書事、都督中外諸軍事，樞密使如故。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitan made Heng Prefecture the central capital. Hanlin Academician Zhang Li memorialized proposing the Prince of Yan as central capital garrison commander, Grand Chancellor, recorder of the Masters of Writing affairs, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, with commissioner of military affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had made Hengzhou the central capital. Zhang Li proposed the Prince of Yan as central capital commander, grand chancellor, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and commander of all armies, retaining his post as commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 契丹主取筆塗去「錄尚書事都督中外諸軍事」而行之。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor took the brush and crossed out "recorder of the Masters of Writing affairs, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad" and issued it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor crossed out "recorder of the Masters of Writing" and "commander of all armies" and issued the rest.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，蜀李繼勳與興州刺史劉景攻固鎮，拔之。

translations.literal: On renxu, Shu's Li Jixun with Xingzhou prefect Liu Jing attacked Gu Town and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Li Jixun of Shu and Liu Jing of Xingzhou attacked Gu Town and captured it.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，何重建請出蜀兵與階成兵共扼散關以取鳳州，丙寅，蜀主發山南兵三千七百赴之。

translations.literal: On yichou, He Chongjian requested to send out Shu troops with Jie and Cheng troops jointly to hold Sans Pass and take Feng Prefecture. On bingyin the Shu ruler dispatched three thousand seven hundred southern Shannan troops to go there.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou He Chongjian asked to send Shu troops with Jie and Cheng forces to hold Sans Pass and take Fengzhou. On bingyin the Shu emperor sent thirty-seven hundred southern Shannan troops.

sentences.zh: 劉知遠聞何重建降蜀，歎曰：「戎狄憑陵，中原無主，令籓鎮外附，吾為方伯，良可愧也！」

translations.literal: Liu Zhiyuan heard He Chongjian had submitted to Shu and sighed: "Barbarians rely on force to overrun us; the central plains have no master; now frontier commands attach to outsiders—I am a regional lord—how shameful!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing He Chongjian had gone over to Shu, Liu Zhiyuan sighed, "Barbarians overrun us, the central plains have no ruler, and frontier commands turn elsewhere—a regional lord like me should be ashamed!

sentences.zh: 於是將佐勸知遠稱尊號，以號令四方，觀諸侯去就。

translations.literal: Thereupon his generals and aides urged Zhiyuan to assume an exalted title to command the four directions and observe the feudal lords' coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged him to take the throne, command the realm, and watch which lords would follow.

sentences.zh: 知遠不許。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan refused.

sentences.zh: 聞晉主北還，聲言欲出兵井陘，迎歸晉陽。

translations.literal: Hearing the Jin emperor was returning north, he proclaimed he wished to send troops through Jingxing Pass to welcome him back to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the Jin emperor was marching north, he announced he would march through Jingxing Pass to welcome him home to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，命武節都指揮使滎澤史弘肇集諸軍於球場，告以出師之期。

translations.literal: On dingmao, he ordered Martial Discipline Commander-in-Chief Shi Hongzhao of Rongze to assemble the armies at the ball ground and announce the date for marching out.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he ordered Shi Hongzhao of Rongze, commander of martial discipline, to rally the armies on the drill ground and announce the campaign date.

sentences.zh: 軍士皆曰：「今契丹陷京城，執天子，天下無主。

translations.literal: The soldiers all said: "Now the Khitan have seized the capital, hold the Son of Heaven, and all under heaven has no master.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers cried, "The Khitan hold the capital and the emperor—the realm has no ruler.

sentences.zh: 主天下者，非我王而誰！

translations.literal: To master all under heaven—if not our king, then who!
translations.idiomatic: Who should rule if not our lord!

sentences.zh: 宜先正位號，然後出師。」

translations.literal: We ought first to establish the title and position, then march out."
translations.idiomatic: Take the throne first, then march."

sentences.zh: 爭呼萬歲不已。

translations.literal: They competed in shouting "ten thousand years" without cease.
translations.idiomatic: They shouted "Long live the emperor!" without end.

sentences.zh: 知遠曰：「虜勢尚強，吾軍威未振，當且建功業。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan said: "The barbarians' momentum is still strong; our army's prestige is not yet roused—we should first build achievement and enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan said, "The barbarians are still strong and our army's prestige is not yet established—we must win victories first.

sentences.zh: 士卒何知！」

translations.literal: What do common soldiers know!"
translations.idiomatic: What do common soldiers know!"

sentences.zh: 命左右遏止之。

translations.literal: He ordered those at his side to restrain and stop them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to silence them.

sentences.zh: 己巳，行軍司馬潞城張彥威等三上箋勸進，知遠疑未決。

translations.literal: On jisi, Marching Army Vice Commander Zhang Yanwei of Lucheng and others three times submitted memorials urging assumption of the throne; Zhiyuan hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Zhang Yanwei of Lucheng and others thrice urged him to take the throne; Zhiyuan still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 郭威與都押牙冠氏楊邠入說知遠曰：「今遠近之心，不謀而同，此天意也。

translations.literal: Guo Wei with Chief Military Aide Yang Bin of Guanshi entered to persuade Zhiyuan: "Now hearts near and far, without plotting, are the same—this is heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei and Yang Bin of Guanshi urged Zhiyuan, "Hearts near and far agree without collusion—this is heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 王不乘此際取之，謙讓不居，恐人心且移，移則反受其咎矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness does not seize it at this juncture and through modest yielding does not occupy it, I fear people's hearts will shift; once shifted, you will instead receive blame."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not seize this moment through modesty, hearts will shift—and you will pay for it."

sentences.zh: 知遠從之。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 契丹以其將劉願為保義節度副使，陝人苦其暴虐。

translations.literal: The Khitan made their general Liu Yuan vice military governor of Baoyi; the people of Shaan suffered under his cruelty and tyranny.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan made their general Liu Yuan vice governor of Baoyi; the people of Shaan groaned under his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 奉國都頭王晏與指揮使趙暉、都頭侯章謀曰：「今胡虜亂華，乃吾屬奮發之秋。

translations.literal: Fengguo company commander Wang Yan with Commander Zhao Hui and company commander Hou Zhang plotted, saying: "Now the barbarians disorder China—this is the season for us to rouse ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan of Fengguo, Zhao Hui, and Hou Zhang plotted together: "The barbarians ravage China—this is our hour to act.

sentences.zh: 河東劉公，威德遠著，吾輩若殺願，舉陝城歸之，為天下唱，取富貴如反掌耳。」

translations.literal: Lord Liu of Hedong—his prestige and virtue are renowned afar. If we kill Yuan, raise Shaan city and submit to him, take the lead for all under heaven—gaining wealth and rank will be like turning the hand."
translations.idiomatic: Lord Liu of Hedong is famed far and wide. Kill Yuan, surrender Shaan to him, lead the realm—and fortune will be ours in a stroke."

sentences.zh: 暉等然之。

translations.literal: Hui and the others assented.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 晏與壯士數人，夜逾牙城入府，出庫兵以給眾。

translations.literal: Yan with several stalwart men at night crossed the yamen wall into the headquarters, took out armory weapons to supply the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and a few bold men scaled the yamen wall by night, entered the headquarters, and issued arms from the storehouse.

sentences.zh: 庚午旦，斬願首，懸諸府門，又殺契丹監軍，奉暉為留後。

translations.literal: At dawn on gengwu they beheaded Yuan and hung his head at the headquarters gate, also killed the Khitan army supervisor, and elevated Hui as acting garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on gengwu they beheaded Yuan and hung his head at the gate, killed the Khitan supervisor, and made Hui acting commander.

sentences.zh: 晏，徐州；

translations.literal: Yan was from Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yan was from Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 暉，澶州；

translations.literal: Hui from Dan Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Hui from Danzhou;

sentences.zh: 章，太原人也。

translations.literal: Zhang was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 辛未，劉知遠即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Liu Zhiyuan assumed the emperor's position.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Liu Zhiyuan took the throne.

sentences.zh: 自言未忍改晉國，又惡開運之名，乃更稱天福十二年。

translations.literal: He himself said he could not bear to change the Jin state, and also detested the name Kaiyun, so he again called it the twelfth year of Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: He said he could not bear to abolish Jin and hated the era name Kaiyun, so he proclaimed the twelfth year of Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 壬申，詔：「諸道為契丹括錢率帛者，皆罷之。

translations.literal: On renshen, an edict: "All circuits that forced loans of money and silk for the Khitan—all are abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen an edict abolished all forced Khitan levies of money and silk in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 其晉臣被迫脅為使者勿問，令詣行在。

translations.literal: Jin ministers who were compelled and coerced to serve as envoys—do not question them; order them to come to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Jin officials forced to serve as Khitan envoys were pardoned and ordered to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 自餘契丹，所在誅之。」

translations.literal: As for remaining Khitan, wherever found execute them."
translations.idiomatic: All other Khitan found anywhere were to be killed."

sentences.zh: 何重建遣宮苑使崔延琛將兵攻鳳州，不克，退保固鎮。

translations.literal: He Chongjian sent Palace Gardens Commissioner Cui Yanchen to lead troops to attack Feng Prefecture; they did not overcome it and withdrew to hold Gu Town.
translations.idiomatic: He Chongjian sent Cui Yanchen to attack Fengzhou but failed and fell back to Gu Town.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝自將東迎晉主及太后。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the emperor personally led troops east to welcome the Jin emperor and empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the emperor marched east in person to welcome the Jin emperor and dowager.

sentences.zh: 至壽陽，聞已過恆州數日，乃留兵戍承天軍而還。

translations.literal: Reaching Shouyang, he heard they had passed Heng Prefecture several days before; he then left troops to garrison Chengtian Army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouyang he learned they had passed Hengzhou days before; he garrisoned Chengtian Army and turned back.

sentences.zh: 晉主既出寨，契丹無復供給，從官、宮女，皆自采木實、草葉而食之。

translations.literal: After the Jin emperor had left the stockade, the Khitan made no further supplies; attendants and palace women all gathered tree fruit and grass leaves themselves to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jin emperor left camp, the Khitan gave nothing more; attendants and palace women gathered wild fruit and leaves to eat.

sentences.zh: 至錦州，契丹令晉主及后妃拜契丹主阿保機墓。

translations.literal: Reaching Jin Prefecture, the Khitan ordered the Jin emperor and consorts to bow at the tomb of Khitan ruler Abaoji.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinzhou the Khitan forced the Jin emperor and his consorts to bow at Abaoji's tomb.

sentences.zh: 晉主不勝屈辱，泣曰：「薛超誤我！」

translations.literal: The Jin emperor could not bear the humiliation and wept, saying: "Xue Chao misled me!"
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor wept under the humiliation: "Xue Chao ruined me!

sentences.zh: 馮后陰令左右求毒藥，欲與晉主俱自殺，不果。

translations.literal: Empress Feng secretly ordered attendants to seek poison, wishing to kill herself together with the Jin emperor; it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Feng secretly sought poison to die with him but failed.

sentences.zh: 契丹主聞帝即位，以通事耿崇美為昭義節度使，高唐英為彰德節度使，崔廷勳為河陽節度使，以控扼要害。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor heard the emperor had assumed the throne and made interpreter Geng Chongmei military governor of Zhaoyi, Gao Tangying of Zhangde, and Cui Tingxun of Heyang to control strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the enthronement, the Khitan emperor posted Geng Chongmei at Zhaoyi, Gao Tangying at Zhangde, and Cui Tingxun at Heyang to hold key points.

sentences.zh: 初，晉置鄉兵，號天威軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jin established local militia called the Army of Heavenly Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had once raised local militia called the Army of Heavenly Prestige.

sentences.zh: 教習歲餘，村民不閒軍旅，竟不可用。

translations.literal: After more than a year of instruction, village people were unaccustomed to military affairs and in the end could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: After a year of drill the villagers were still unfit for war and proved useless.

sentences.zh: 悉罷之，但令七戶輸錢十千，其鎧仗悉輸官。

translations.literal: All were dismissed; only seven households were ordered to pay ten thousand cash, and all their armor and weapons were delivered to the government.
translations.idiomatic: They were all disbanded; every seven households paid ten thousand cash and surrendered all arms to the state.

sentences.zh: 而無賴子弟，不復肯復農業，山林之盜，自是而繁。

translations.literal: Yet ruffian sons and younger brothers were no longer willing to return to farming; mountain-forest bandits from this became numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Idle young men refused farming; mountain bandits multiplied from then on.

sentences.zh: 及契丹入汴，縱胡騎打草穀。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, they let Khitan cavalry "beat the grass for grain."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian they let horsemen loot under the name of grazing.

sentences.zh: 又多以其子弟及親信左右為節度使、刺史，不通政事，華人之狡獪者多往依其麾下，教之妄作威福，掊斂貨財，民不堪命。

translations.literal: They also often made their sons and younger brothers and trusted close attendants military governors and prefects, ignorant of government affairs; many crafty Han went to rely under their banners, teaching them to wield authority and blessings wantonly, extorting goods and wealth—the people could not bear their orders.
translations.idiomatic: They installed sons and favorites as governors and prefects who knew no governance; crafty Han flocked to them, taught them to abuse power and squeeze the people past endurance.

sentences.zh: 於是所在相聚為盜，多者數萬人，少者不減千百，攻陷州縣，殺掠吏民。

translations.literal: Thereupon everywhere people gathered as bandits—many groups tens of thousands, few not less than hundreds or thousands—storming prefectures and counties, killing and plundering officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere bands formed—some tens of thousands strong, none fewer than hundreds—storming counties, killing officials, and looting the people.

sentences.zh: 滏陽賊帥梁暉，有眾數百，送款晉陽求效用，帝許之。

translations.literal: Fuyang bandit chief Liang Hui had a force of several hundred, sent allegiance to Jinyang seeking employment, and the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hui of Fuyang, with several hundred men, submitted to Jinyang for service and the emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 磁州刺史李穀密通表於帝，令暉襲相州。

translations.literal: Cizhou prefect Li Gu secretly sent a memorial to the emperor ordering Hui to strike Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu of Cizhou secretly urged the emperor to have Hui seize Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 暉偵知高唐英未至，相州積兵器，無守備。

translations.literal: Hui spied and learned Gao Tangying had not yet arrived; Xiang Prefecture had stored weapons but no defense preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Hui learned Gao Tangying had not yet arrived and that Xiangzhou held arms but no garrison.

sentences.zh: 丁丑夜，遣壯士逾城入，啟關納其眾，殺契丹數百，其守將突圍走，暉據州自稱留後，表言其狀。

translations.literal: On the night of dingchou he sent stalwarts over the wall to enter, opened the gate to admit his force, killed several hundred Khitan; the defending general broke out and fled. Hui held the prefecture, declared himself acting commander, and memorialized the situation.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of dingchou his men scaled the wall, opened the gates, killed hundreds of Khitan, and drove the defender out. Hui seized the city, declared himself acting commander, and reported to court.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，帝還至晉陽，議率民財以賞將士，夫人李氏諫曰：「陛下因河東創大業，未有以惠澤其民，而先奪其生生之資，殆非新天子所以救民之意也。

translations.literal: On wuyin the emperor returned to Jinyang and discussed levying the people's wealth to reward officers and soldiers. Lady Li remonstrated: "Your Majesty, through Hedong, founded the great enterprise and has not yet shown favor and grace to the people, yet first seizes the resources by which they live—this is hardly the intent of a new Son of Heaven to save the people.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the emperor returned to Jinyang and planned to levy the people's wealth for the army. Lady Li objected: "You built your enterprise in Hedong without yet blessing the people—seizing their livelihood first is hardly how a new emperor saves his subjects.

sentences.zh: 今宮中所有，請悉出之以勞軍，雖復不厚，人無怨言。」

translations.literal: What the palace now holds—please bring it all out to comfort the army; though it may not again be generous, the people will have no complaints of grievance."
translations.idiomatic: Give all we have in the palace to reward the troops—even if it is not much, no one will complain."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said!

sentences.zh: 即罷率民，傾內府蓄積以賜將士，中外聞之，大悅。

translations.literal: He immediately stopped levying the people, poured out the inner treasury's accumulations to bestow on officers and soldiers; inside and outside hearing this were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the levy, emptied the inner treasury for the troops, and all rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 李氏，晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Lady Li was a native of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 吳越內都監程昭悅，多聚賓客，畜兵器，與術士游。

translations.literal: Wuyue's Inner Capital Supervisor Cheng Zhaoyue gathered many guests, stored weapons, and associated with occult masters.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhaoyue, Wuyue's inner capital supervisor, gathered guests, hoarded arms, and consorted with occultists.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘佐欲誅之，謂水丘昭券曰：「汝今夕帥甲士千人圍昭悅第。」

translations.literal: King Hongzuo of Wuyue wished to execute him and said to Shuiqiu Zhaoquan: "You tonight lead a thousand armored soldiers to surround Zhaoyue's residence."
translations.idiomatic: King Hongzuo of Wuyue meant to kill him and told Shuiqiu Zhaoquan, "Tonight lead a thousand soldiers to surround Zhaoyue's house.

sentences.zh: 昭券曰：「昭悅，家臣也，有罪當顯戮，不宜夜興兵。」

translations.literal: Zhaoquan said: "Zhaoyue is a household minister; if guilty he should be openly executed—it is not fitting to raise troops at night."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoquan replied, "Zhaoyue is a household servant; if guilty he should be executed openly—not by night attacks."

sentences.zh: 弘佐曰：「善！」

translations.literal: Hongzuo said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo said, "Good!

sentences.zh: 命內牙指揮使儲溫伺昭悅歸第，執送東府，己卯，斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered Inner Guard Commander Chu Wen to watch for Zhaoyue's return home, seize and send him to the Eastern Headquarters; on jimao he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He had Inner Guard Commander Chu Wen seize Zhaoyue when he returned home and sent him to the eastern headquarters; on jimao he was executed.

sentences.zh: 釋錢仁俊之囚。

translations.literal: He released Qian Renjun from imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: He freed Qian Renjun from prison.

sentences.zh: 武節都指揮使史弘肇攻代州，拔之，斬王暉。

translations.literal: Martial Discipline Commander-in-Chief Shi Hongzhao attacked Dai Prefecture, took it, and beheaded Wang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao attacked Daizhou, captured it, and beheaded Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 建雄留後劉在明朝於契丹，以節度副使駱從朗知州事。

translations.literal: Jianxiong acting commander Liu Zaili went to court before the Khitan and made vice military governor Luo Conglang handle prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zaili of Jianxiong went to Khitan court and left Luo Conglang as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者張晏洪等如晉州，諭以己即帝位，從朗皆囚之。
