translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys Zhang Yanhong and others to Jin Prefecture to announce he had assumed the throne; Conglang imprisoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zhang Yanhong and others to Jinzhou to announce his enthronement; Conglang imprisoned them all.

sentences.zh: 大將藥可儔殺從朗，推晏洪權留後，庚辰，遣使以聞。

translations.literal: Great general Yao Keyou killed Conglang, elevated Yanhong as acting commander; on gengchen he sent envoys to report.
translations.idiomatic: General Yao Keyou killed Conglang, made Yanhong acting commander, and on gengchen reported to court.

sentences.zh: 契丹主遣右諫議大夫趙熙使晉州，括率錢帛，征督甚急。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor sent Right Remonstrating Grandee Zhao Xi as envoy to Jin Prefecture to force loans of money and silk, collecting and supervising with extreme urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor sent Zhao Xi to Jinzhou to levy money and silk with brutal urgency.

sentences.zh: 從朗既死，民相帥共殺熙。

translations.literal: After Conglang was dead, the people led one another and together killed Xi.
translations.idiomatic: After Conglang's death the people rose together and killed Xi.

sentences.zh: 契丹主賜趙暉詔，即以為保義留後。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor bestowed an edict on Zhao Hui and immediately made him acting Baoyi commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor issued an edict making Zhao Hui acting governor of Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 暉斬契丹使者，焚其詔，遣支使河間趙矩奉表詣晉陽。

translations.literal: Hui beheaded the Khitan envoy, burned the edict, and sent staff officer Zhao Ju of Hejian to present a memorial to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hui killed the Khitan envoy, burned the edict, and sent Zhao Ju of Hejian to Jinyang with a pledge of allegiance.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣其將高模翰攻暉，不克。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent their general Gao Mohan to attack Hui but did not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent Gao Mohan against him but failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 帝見矩，甚喜，曰：「子挈咽喉之地以歸我，天下不足定也！」

translations.literal: The emperor saw Ju and was greatly pleased, saying: "You have brought the throat region back to me—all under heaven will not be hard to settle!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received Ju with delight and said, "You bring the throat of the realm back to me—the empire is half won!

sentences.zh: 矩因勸帝早引兵南向以副天下之望，帝善之。

translations.literal: Ju thereupon urged the emperor early to lead troops south to match all under heaven's hopes; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Ju urged an early march south to meet the realm's hopes, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以暉為保義節度使，侯章為鎮國節度使、保義軍馬步都指揮使，王晏為絳州防禦使、保義軍馬步副指揮使。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Hui was made military governor of Baoyi; Hou Zhang military governor of Zhenguo and Baoyi army infantry and cavalry commander-in-chief; Wang Yan defense commissioner of Jiang Prefecture and Baoyi army infantry and cavalry vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Hui was made governor of Baoyi; Hou Zhang governor of Zhenguo and commander of Baoyi forces; Wang Yan defense commissioner of Jiangzhou and vice commander.

sentences.zh: 高防與王守恩謀，遣指揮使李萬超白晝帥眾大噪入府，斬趙行遷，推守恩權知昭義留後。

translations.literal: Gao Fang and Wang Shou'en plotted, sending Commander Li Wanchao in broad daylight to lead the crowd with great clamor into the headquarters, behead Zhao Xingqian, and elevate Shou'en as acting Zhaoyi commander.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Fang and Wang Shou'en sent Li Wanchao to storm the headquarters in daylight, kill Zhao Xingqian, and make Shou'en acting Zhaoyi commander.

sentences.zh: 守恩殺契丹使者，舉鎮來降。

translations.literal: Shou'en killed the Khitan envoy and raised the whole command to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shou'en killed the Khitan envoy and surrendered the whole command.

sentences.zh: 鎮寧節度使耶律郎五，性殘虐，澶州人苦之。

translations.literal: Zhenning military governor Yelü Langwu's nature was cruel and tyrannical; the people of Dan Prefecture suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Langwu of Zhenning was cruel; the people of Danzhou suffered terribly.

sentences.zh: 賊帥王瓊帥其徒千餘人，夜襲據南城，北度浮航，縱兵大掠，圍郎五於牙城。

translations.literal: Bandit chief Wang Qiong led his band of more than a thousand; at night they raided and seized the south city, crossed north over the pontoon bridge, let troops plunder greatly, and besieged Langwu in the yamen city.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chief Wang Qiong led more than a thousand men in a night raid on the south city, crossed the pontoon bridge, looted freely, and besieged Langwu in his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 契丹主聞之，甚懼，始遣天平節度使李守貞、天雄節度使杜重威還鎮，由是無久留河南之意。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor heard this and was greatly afraid; he first sent Pingheng military governor Li Shouzhen and Tianxiong military governor Du Chongwei back to their posts—from this he had no intent to stay long south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor was alarmed and sent Li Shouzhen and Du Chongwei back to their posts—he no longer meant to linger south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 遣兵救澶州，瓊退屯近郊，遣其弟超奉表來求救。

translations.literal: He sent troops to rescue Dan Prefecture; Qiong withdrew to encamp in the near suburbs and sent his younger brother Chao to present a memorial seeking rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to relieve Danzhou; Qiong withdrew to the suburbs and sent his brother Chao to plead for aid.

sentences.zh: 癸未，帝厚賜超，遣還。

translations.literal: On guimao the emperor richly rewarded Chao and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the emperor richly rewarded Chao and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 瓊兵敗，為契丹所殺。

translations.literal: Qiong's troops were defeated and he was killed by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was defeated and killed by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 蜀主加雄武節度使何重建同平章事。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler added Xiongwu military governor He Chongjian as concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu emperor made He Chongjian of Xiongwu a grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 延州錄事參軍高允權，萬金之子也。

translations.literal: Yanzhou recording adjutant Gao Yunquan was the son of Wan Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yunquan, recording adjutant of Yanzhou, was Wan Jin's son.

sentences.zh: 彰武節度使周密，暗而貪，將士作亂，攻之。

translations.literal: Zhangwu military governor Zhou Mi was dim-witted and greedy; officers and soldiers mutinied and attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mi of Zhangwu was dull and greedy; his troops mutinied and attacked him.

sentences.zh: 密敗，保東城。

translations.literal: Mi was defeated and held the east city.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was beaten back and held the east city.

sentences.zh: 眾以允權家世延帥，推為留後，據西城。

translations.literal: The crowd, because Yunquan's family for generations had been Yan commanders, elevated him as acting commander and held the west city.
translations.idiomatic: The troops, knowing Yunquan's family had long ruled Yan, made him acting commander and held the west city.

sentences.zh: 密，應州人也。

translations.literal: Mi was a man of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was from Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 丹州都指揮使高彥珣殺契丹所署刺史，自領州事。

translations.literal: Dan Prefecture commander-in-chief Gao Yanxun killed the Khitan-appointed prefect and himself assumed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanxun of Danzhou killed the Khitan-appointed prefect and took command himself.

sentences.zh: 契丹述律太后遣使以其國中酒饌脯果賜契丹主，賀平晉國。

translations.literal: Khitan Empress Dowager Shulü sent envoys with wine, delicacies, dried meats, and fruits from their state to bestow on the Khitan emperor, congratulating the pacification of the Jin state.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Shulü sent wine, delicacies, dried meats, and fruit from home to congratulate the Khitan emperor on conquering Jin.

sentences.zh: 契丹主與群臣宴於永福殿，每舉酒，立而飲之，曰：「太后所賜，不敢坐飲。」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor banqueted with his ministers in the Hall of Eternal Blessings; each time he raised wine he stood to drink it, saying: "What the empress dowager bestowed—I dare not drink seated."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor feasted his ministers in the Hall of Eternal Blessings; each time he raised his cup he stood and said, "A gift from the empress dowager—I dare not drink seated."

sentences.zh: 唐王淑妃與郇公從益居洛陽。

translations.literal: Tang's Honored Consort Wang and Duke of Xun Congyi dwelt in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Honored Consort Wang and Duke of Xun Congyi lived in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽娶明宗女為夫人，淑妃詣大梁會禮。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou married Emperor Mingzong's daughter as his lady; the honored consort went to Daliang to attend the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou had married a daughter of Emperor Mingzong; the honored consort went to Daliang for the rites.

sentences.zh: 契丹主見而拜之曰：「吾嫂也。」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor saw her and bowed, saying: "She is my elder brother's wife."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor bowed to her and said, "She is my sister-in-law."

sentences.zh: 統軍劉遂凝因淑妃求節鉞，契丹主以從益為許王、威信節度使，遂凝為安遠節度使。

translations.literal: Army commander Liu Suining through the honored consort sought the command baton; the Khitan emperor made Congyi Prince of Xu and Weixin military governor, and Suining Anyuan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Liu Suining sought a command through her; the Khitan emperor made Congyi Prince of Xu and governor of Weixin, and Suining governor of Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 淑妃以從益幼，辭不赴鎮，復歸於洛。

translations.literal: The honored consort, because Congyi was young, declined and did not go to his post, returning again to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The honored consort declined the post for young Congyi and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 契丹主以張礪為右僕射兼門下侍郎、同平章事，左僕射和凝兼中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor made Zhang Li Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing with concurrent Gate Department Attendant and Grand Councilor; Left Vice Director He Ning with concurrent Secretariat Attendant and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor made Zhang Li right vice director of the Masters of Writing with grand councilor rank, and He Ning left vice director with the same.

sentences.zh: 司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事劉昫，以目疾辭位，罷為太保。

translations.literal: Minister of Works with concurrent Gate Department Attendant and Grand Councilor Liu Xu, on account of eye disease resigned his post and was removed to Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu, minister of works and grand councilor, resigned for eye disease and was made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 東方群盜大起，陷宋、亳、密三州。

translations.literal: Bandit groups in the east rose greatly, seizing Song, Bo, and Mi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose across the east and seized Song, Bo, and Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹主謂左右曰：「我不知中國之人難制如此！」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor said to those at his side: "I did not know the people of China were so hard to control!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor told his attendants, "I never knew Chinese were so hard to control!

sentences.zh: 亟遣泰寧節度使安審琦、武寧節度使符彥卿等歸鎮，仍以契丹兵送之。

translations.literal: He hastily sent Taining military governor An Shenqi, Wuning military governor Fu Yanqing, and others back to their posts, still using Khitan troops to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: He hastily sent An Shenqi of Taining, Fu Yanqing of Wuning, and others back to their posts with Khitan escorts.

sentences.zh: 彥卿至埇橋，賊帥李仁恕帥眾數萬急攻徐州。

translations.literal: Yanqing reached Yong Bridge; bandit chief Li Renshu led a force of tens of thousands urgently attacking Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Yong Bridge Yanqing found Li Renshu leading tens of thousands in a furious assault on Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥卿與數十騎至城下，揚鞭欲招諭之，仁恕控彥卿馬，請從相公入城。

translations.literal: Yanqing with several dozen horsemen reached below the city, raised his whip wishing to summon and persuade them; Renshu seized Yanqing's horse and requested he follow the chief minister into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing rode to the walls with a few dozen men and raised his whip to parley; Renshu seized his horse and asked him to enter the city.

sentences.zh: 彥卿子昭序，自城中遣軍校陳守習縋而出，呼於賊中曰：「相公已陷虎口，聽相公助賊攻城，城不可得也。」

translations.literal: Yanqing's son Zhaoxu from within the city sent army officer Chen Shouxi lowered by rope outside, calling among the bandits: "The chief minister has already fallen into the tiger's mouth; if you listen to the chief minister helping bandits attack the city, the city cannot be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing's son Zhaoxu lowered Chen Shouxi by rope from the city and shouted to the bandits, "My father is in your hands—if he helps you attack, you will never take the city.

sentences.zh: 賊知不可劫，乃相帥羅拜於彥卿馬前，乞赦其罪。

translations.literal: The bandits knew they could not seize him and thereupon led one another in circling bows before Yanqing's horse, begging pardon for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing they could not hold him, the bandits bowed in a ring before Yanqing's horse and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 彥卿與之誓，乃解去。

translations.literal: Yanqing swore with them, and then they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing swore an oath with them and they dispersed.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙戌朔，契丹主服赭袍，坐崇元殿，百官行入閣禮。

translations.literal: Third month, first day of the month bingxu, the Khitan emperor wore ochre robe, sat in the Hall of Exalted Origin, and the hundred officials performed the entering-pavilion ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day bingxu, the Khitan emperor wore an ochre robe, sat in the Hall of Exalted Origin, and officials performed the entering-pavilion ceremony.

sentences.zh: 戊子，帝遣使以詔書安集農民保聚山谷避契丹之患者。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the emperor sent envoys with an edict to settle and gather farmers who had gathered in mountain valleys to escape those suffering from the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the emperor sent edicts to reassure farmers who had fled to the hills from the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，高允權奉表來降。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Gao Yunquan presented a memorial coming to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Gao Yunquan submitted his allegiance.

sentences.zh: 帝諭允權聽周密詣行在，密遂棄東城來奔。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed Yunquan to permit Zhou Mi to come to the mobile court; Mi thereupon abandoned the east city and came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yunquan to let Zhou Mi come to court; Mi abandoned the east city and fled to him.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，高彥詢以丹州來降。

translations.literal: On renchen, Gao Yanxun surrendered Dan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Gao Yanxun surrendered Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀翰林承旨李昊謂樞密使王處回曰：「敵復據固鎮，則興州道絕，不復能救秦州矣。

translations.literal: Shu Hanlin Academician Li Hao said to Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Chuhui: "If the enemy again holds Gu Town, the road to Xing Prefecture will be cut and we will no longer be able to rescue Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hao of Shu told Wang Chuhui, commissioner of military affairs, "If the enemy holds Gu Town again, the road to Xingzhou will be cut and Qinzhou cannot be saved.

sentences.zh: 請遣山南西道節度使孫漢韶將兵急攻鳳州。」

translations.literal: Please send Shannan West Circuit military governor Sun Hanshao to lead troops urgently to attack Feng Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Send Sun Hanshao of Shannan West Circuit to strike Fengzhou at once."

sentences.zh: 癸巳，蜀主命漢韶詣鳳州行營。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Shu ruler ordered Hanshao to go to Feng Prefecture's campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the Shu emperor ordered Hanshao to the Fengzhou front.

sentences.zh: 契丹主復召晉百官，諭之曰：「天時向暑，吾難久留，欲暫至上國省太后。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor again summoned Jin's hundred officials and announced to them: "Heaven's season turns hot—I can hardly stay long. I wish temporarily to go to the northern state to visit the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor summoned the Jin officials again and said, "Summer is coming—I cannot stay long. I will visit the empress dowager in the north.

sentences.zh: 當留親信一人於此為節度使。」

translations.literal: I ought to leave one trusted intimate here as military governor."
translations.idiomatic: I will leave a trusted man here as governor."

sentences.zh: 百官請迎太后。

translations.literal: The hundred officials requested welcoming the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The officials asked him to bring the empress dowager south.

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「太后族大，如古柏根，不可移也。」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor said: "The empress dowager's clan is great, like the root of an ancient cypress—it cannot be moved."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor said, "The empress dowager's clan is vast, like the roots of an ancient cypress—it cannot be moved."

sentences.zh: 契丹主欲盡以晉之百官自隨。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor wished to take all Jin's hundred officials with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor wanted to take all Jin officials with him.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「舉國北遷，恐搖人心，不如稍稍遷之。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Moving the whole state north will fear shaking people's hearts—better to move them little by little."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Moving the whole court north would shake hearts—better to move them gradually."

sentences.zh: 乃詔有職事者從行，餘留大梁。

translations.literal: An edict was issued that those with official duties should follow on the journey; the rest remained at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered officials with duties to accompany him and left the rest at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 復以汴州為宣武軍，以蕭翰為節度使。

translations.literal: He again made Bian Prefecture the Xuanwu Army and made Xiao Han military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Bianzhou as the Xuanwu command and made Xiao Han its governor.

sentences.zh: 翰，述律太后之兄子，其妹復為契丹主後。

translations.literal: Han was Empress Dowager Shulü's elder brother's son; his younger sister again became the Khitan emperor's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Han was a nephew of Empress Dowager Shulü; his sister again became the Khitan emperor's consort.

sentences.zh: 翰始以蕭為姓，自是契丹後族皆稱蕭氏。

translations.literal: Han first took Xiao as surname; from this Khitan consort clans all were called the Xiao house.
translations.idiomatic: Han first took the surname Xiao; thereafter Khitan consort clans all bore the name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 吳越復發水軍，遣其將余安將之，自海道救福州。

translations.literal: Wuyue again launched a naval force, sending their general Yu An to command it, rescuing Fuzhou by the sea route.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyue sent another fleet under Yu An to relieve Fuzhou by sea.

sentences.zh: 己亥，至白蝦浦。

translations.literal: On jihai they reached White Shrimp Creek.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai they reached White Shrimp Creek.

sentences.zh: 海岸泥淖，須布竹簀乃可行，唐之諸軍在城南者，聚而射之，簀不得施。

translations.literal: The coast was muddy slough; they had to lay bamboo mats before they could advance. Tang armies south of the city gathered and shot at them; the mats could not be deployed.
translations.idiomatic: The coast was mud; they had to lay bamboo matting to advance. Tang troops south of the city shot at them and prevented it.

sentences.zh: 馮延魯曰：「城所以不降者，恃此救也。

translations.literal: Feng Yanlu said: "The reason the city does not surrender is that it relies on this rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanlu said, "The city holds out only because it expects this relief.

sentences.zh: 今相持不戰，徒老我師，不若縱其登岸盡殺之，則城不攻自降矣。」

translations.literal: Now if we stand facing each other without fighting, we only wear out our army in vain—better to let them come ashore and kill them all, then the city will surrender without attack."
translations.idiomatic: If we stand idle we only weary our army—let them land and slaughter them all, and the city will fall without a siege."

sentences.zh: 裨將孟堅曰：「浙兵至此已久，不能進退，求一戰而死不可得。

translations.literal: Vice general Meng Jian said: "The Zhe troops have been here long, unable to advance or retreat—they cannot even obtain death in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Vice general Meng Jian objected, "The Zhe troops have been stuck here so long they would die fighting—

sentences.zh: 若聽其登岸，彼必致死於我，其鋒不可當，安能盡殺乎！」

translations.literal: If we let them come ashore, they will surely fight to the death against us—their edge cannot be withstood; how could we kill them all!"
translations.idiomatic: if we let them land they will fight to the death and we cannot withstand them—how could we kill them all!

sentences.zh: 延魯不聽，曰：「吾自擊之。」

translations.literal: Yanlu would not listen and said: "I myself will strike them."
translations.idiomatic: Yanlu would not listen. "I will attack them myself."

sentences.zh: 吳越兵既登岸，大呼奮擊，延魯不能御，棄眾而走，孟堅戰死。

translations.literal: Once Wuyue troops had come ashore, they shouted loudly and struck fiercely; Yanlu could not withstand them, abandoned the crowd and fled; Meng Jian died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuyue troops landed they charged with a roar. Yanlu could not hold them, fled, and Meng Jian was killed.

sentences.zh: 吳越兵乘勝而進，城中兵亦出，夾擊唐兵，大破之。

translations.literal: Wuyue troops pressed the victory; city troops also came out, attacking Tang troops from both sides, and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuyue troops pressed their advantage; garrison troops sallied out, and together they shattered the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 唐城南諸軍皆遁，吳越兵追之。

translations.literal: All Tang armies south of the city fled; Wuyue troops pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: Tang forces south of the city fled; the Wuyue troops pursued.

sentences.zh: 王崇文以牙兵三百拒之，諸軍陳於崇文之後，追者乃還。

translations.literal: Wang Chongwen with three hundred guard troops resisted them; the various armies formed battle lines behind Chongwen, and the pursuers then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongwen held them off with three hundred guards; the other armies formed behind him and the pursuers withdrew.

sentences.zh: 或言浙兵欲棄福州，拔李達之眾歸錢唐。

translations.literal: Someone said the Zhe troops wished to abandon Fuzhou, pull out Li Da's force, and return to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Some said the Zhe troops meant to abandon Fuzhou, take Li Da's men, and return to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 東南守將劉洪進等白王建封，請縱其盡出而取其城。

translations.literal: Southeast garrison generals Liu Hongjin and others informed Wang Jianfeng, requesting to let them all come out and then take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast garrison generals Liu Hongjin and others told Wang Jianfeng they should let the enemy leave and then take the city.

sentences.zh: 留從效不欲福州之平，建封亦忿陳覺等專橫，乃曰：「吾軍敗矣，安能與人爭城！」

translations.literal: Liu Congxiao did not wish Fuzhou pacified; Jianfeng also resented Chen Jue and others' domineering arrogance, and said: "Our army is defeated—how can we contend with others for a city!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congxiao did not want Fuzhou pacified; Jianfeng also resented Chen Jue's arrogance and said, "We are beaten—how can we fight for the city!

sentences.zh: 是夕，燒營而遁，城北諸軍亦相顧而潰。

translations.literal: That evening they burned camp and fled; armies north of the city also looked at one another and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: That night they burned camp and fled; northern armies broke and ran as well.

sentences.zh: 馮延魯引佩刀自刺，親吏救之，不死。

translations.literal: Feng Yanlu drew his belt dagger to stab himself; close attendants saved him and he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanlu tried to kill himself with his dagger; attendants saved him.

sentences.zh: 唐兵死者二萬餘人，委棄軍資器械數十萬，府庫為之耗竭。

translations.literal: Tang troops dead numbered more than twenty thousand; they abandoned hundreds of thousands of military supplies and weapons; treasuries were exhausted by this.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty thousand Tang soldiers died; they abandoned vast stores of arms and supplies and emptied the treasury.

sentences.zh: 余安引兵入福州，李達舉所部授之。

translations.literal: Yu An led troops into Fuzhou; Li Da presented his entire command to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu An entered Fuzhou and Li Da surrendered his entire command.

sentences.zh: 留從效引兵還泉州，謂唐戍將曰：「泉州與福州世為仇敵，南接嶺海瘴癘之鄉，地險土瘠。

translations.literal: Liu Congxiao led troops back to Quan Prefecture and said to Tang garrison generals: "Quan and Fuzhou for generations have been mutual foes; south they connect to the miasmic lands of the Ling mountains and sea; the terrain is dangerous and soil poor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congxiao returned to Quanzhou and told the Tang garrison, "Quanzhou and Fuzhou have been enemies for generations. South lies the malarial coast; the land is rugged and poor.

sentences.zh: 比年軍旅屢興，農桑廢業，冬征夏斂，僅能自贍，豈勞大軍久戍於此！」

translations.literal: In recent years armies repeatedly rose; farming and sericulture were abandoned; winter campaigns and summer levies barely sufficed for self-support—how could we trouble a great army to garrison here long!"
translations.idiomatic: Years of war have ruined farming; we barely feed ourselves with winter campaigns and summer levies—why should a great army linger here!

sentences.zh: 置酒餞之，戍將不得已引兵歸。

translations.literal: He set out wine to send them off; the garrison generals had no choice but to lead troops back.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted them farewell; the garrison had no choice but to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 唐主不能制，加從效檢校太傅。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler could not control him and added Congxiao as acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor could not restrain him and made him acting grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，契丹主發大梁，晉文武諸司從者數千人，諸軍吏卒又數千人，宮女、宦官數百人，盡載府庫之實以行，所留樂器儀仗而已。

translations.literal: On renyin the Khitan emperor set out from Daliang; Jin civil and military various offices following numbered several thousand; various army clerks and soldiers again several thousand; palace women and eunuchs several hundred—all loaded treasury goods to go; only musical instruments and ceremonial regalia were left.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the Khitan emperor left Daliang with thousands of Jin officials and soldiers, hundreds of palace women and eunuchs, and all the treasury goods—leaving only instruments and ceremonial regalia.

sentences.zh: 夕宿赤岡，契丹主見村落皆空，命有司發榜數百通，所在招撫百姓，然竟不禁胡騎剽掠。

translations.literal: At evening they lodged at Chigang; the Khitan emperor saw villages and hamlets all empty and ordered officials to issue several hundred notices everywhere to console and gather the people—yet in the end he did not forbid Khitan cavalry plunder.
translations.idiomatic: They camped at Red Mound; seeing empty villages, the Khitan emperor posted hundreds of notices to reassure the people—but still did not stop Khitan looting.

sentences.zh: 丙午，契丹〔主〕自白馬渡河，謂宣徽使高勳曰：「吾在上國，以射獵為樂，至此令人悒悒。

translations.literal: On bingwu the Khitan emperor crossed the river from White Horse and said to Palace Secretariat Commissioner Gao Xun: "In the northern state I take hunting as pleasure—coming here makes one depressed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the Khitan emperor crossed the Yellow River at White Horse and told Gao Xun, "At home I take pleasure in the hunt—here I am heartsick.

sentences.zh: 今得歸，死無恨矣。」

translations.literal: Now that I can return, to die will be without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I can go home, I can die without regret."

sentences.zh: 蜀孫漢韶將兵二萬攻鳳州，軍於固鎮，分兵扼散關以絕援路。

translations.literal: Shu's Sun Hanshao led twenty thousand troops to attack Feng Prefecture, encamped at Gu Town, and divided troops to hold Sans Pass and cut off relief routes.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hanshao of Shu led twenty thousand men against Fengzhou, camped at Gu Town, and blocked Sans Pass to cut off relief.

sentences.zh: 張筠、余安皆還錢唐，吳越王弘佐遣東南安撫使鮑修讓將兵戍福州，以東府安撫使錢弘倧為丞相。

translations.literal: Zhang Yun and Yu An both returned to Qiantang; King Hongzuo of Wuyue sent Southeastern Pacification Commissioner Bao Xiurang to lead troops to garrison Fuzhou and made Eastern Headquarters Pacification Commissioner Qian Hongzong chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun and Yu An returned to Qiantang; King Hongzuo of Wuyue sent Bao Xiurang to garrison Fuzhou and made Qian Hongzong chancellor.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以皇弟北京馬步都指揮使崇行太原尹，知府事。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the emperor's younger brother, Northern Capital infantry and cavalry commander-in-chief Chong, was made Taiyuan mayor and handled prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the emperor's brother Chong, commander of the northern capital forces, was made mayor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，契丹主將攻相州，梁暉請降，契丹主赦之，許以為防禦使。

translations.literal: On xinhai the Khitan emperor was about to attack Xiang Prefecture; Liang Hui requested surrender; the Khitan emperor pardoned him and promised to make him defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, as the Khitan emperor prepared to attack Xiangzhou, Liang Hui offered to surrender; the Khitan emperor pardoned him and promised to make him defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 暉疑其詐，復乘城拒守。

translations.literal: Hui suspected deception and again mounted the walls to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Hui suspected a trick and held the walls again.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己未，未明，契丹主命蕃、漢諸軍急攻相州，食時克之，悉殺城中男子，驅其婦女而北，胡人擲嬰孩於空中，舉刃接之以為樂。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on jiwei before dawn, the Khitan emperor ordered Khitan and Han armies urgently to attack Xiang Prefecture; by mealtime they took it, killed all men in the city, drove the women north. Khitan tossed infants in the air and caught them on blades for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, before dawn on jiwei, Khitan and Han armies stormed Xiangzhou and took it by breakfast. They killed every man, drove the women north, and Khitan soldiers tossed infants in the air and caught them on their blades for sport.

sentences.zh: 留高唐英守相州。

translations.literal: He left Gao Tangying to guard Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He left Gao Tangying to hold Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐英閱城中，遺民男女得七百餘人。

translations.literal: Tangying reviewed the city; surviving men and women obtained were more than seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Tangying counted barely seven hundred survivors in the city.

sentences.zh: 其後節度使王繼弘斂城中髑髏瘞之，凡得十餘萬。

translations.literal: Later military governor Wang Jihong gathered the city's skulls and buried them; in all more than a hundred thousand were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Later Governor Wang Jihong gathered and buried more than a hundred thousand skulls from the city.

sentences.zh: 或告磁州刺史李穀謀舉州應漢，契丹主執而詰之，谷不服，契丹主引手於車中，若取所獲文書者。

translations.literal: Someone reported Cizhou prefect Li Gu plotted to raise the prefecture to respond to Han; the Khitan emperor seized and interrogated him. Gu did not submit; the Khitan emperor reached his hand into the carriage as if taking captured documents.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Li Gu of Cizhou of plotting to surrender to the Han emperor. The Khitan emperor seized and questioned him; Gu denied it, and the emperor reached into his carriage as if for evidence.

sentences.zh: 谷知其詐，因請曰：「必有其驗，乞顯示之。」

translations.literal: Gu knew it was deception and thereupon requested: "There must be proof—please display it."
translations.idiomatic: Gu knew it was a bluff and asked, "If there is proof, show it.

sentences.zh: 凡六詰，谷辭氣不屈，乃釋之。

translations.literal: In all six interrogations Gu's words and spirit did not bend, and he was then released.
translations.idiomatic: Through six rounds of questioning Gu never yielded, and they released him.

sentences.zh: 帝以從弟北京馬軍都指揮使信領義成節度使，充侍衛馬軍都指揮使，武節都指揮使史弘肇領忠武節度使，充步軍都指揮使，右都押牙楊邠權樞密使，蕃漢兵馬都孔目官郭威權副樞密使，兩使都孔目官南樂王章權三司使。

translations.literal: The emperor made his younger cousin Northern Capital horse army commander-in-chief Xin military governor of Yicheng and filled the post of imperial guard horse army commander-in-chief; martial discipline commander Shi Hongzhao military governor of Zhongwu and infantry army commander-in-chief; right chief military aide Yang Bin acting commissioner of military affairs; Khitan-Han army and horse chief clerk Guo Wei acting vice commissioner; both commissions chief clerk Wang Zhang of Nanle acting director of the three offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made his cousin Xin governor of Yicheng and commander of the imperial horse guard; Shi Hongzhao governor of Zhongwu and commander of the foot guard; Yang Bin acting commissioner of military affairs; Guo Wei acting vice commissioner; and Wang Zhang of Nanle acting director of the three offices.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，立魏國夫人李氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On guihai, Lady Li, consort of the State of Wei, was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Lady Li of Wei was made empress.

sentences.zh: 契丹主見所過城邑丘墟，謂蕃、漢群臣曰：「致中國如此，皆燕王之罪也。」

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor saw cities and towns he passed were ruins and said to Khitan and Han ministers: "Bringing China to this—all is the Prince of Yan's crime."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing ruined cities along the way, the Khitan emperor told his ministers, "Reducing China to this is all the Prince of Yan's fault.

sentences.zh: 顧張礪曰：「爾亦有力焉。」

translations.literal: He turned to Zhang Li and said: "You too had force in it."
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Zhang Li and said, "You had a hand in it too."

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝以河東節度判官長安蘇逢吉、觀察判官蘇禹珪為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On jiazi the emperor made Hedong military governor judge Su Fengji of Chang'an and observation judge Su Yugui Secretariat Attendants and Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor made Su Fengji of Chang'an and Su Yugui of Hedong secretariat attendants and grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 禹珪，密州人也。

translations.literal: Yugui was a man of Mi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yugui was from Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 振武節度使、府州團練使折從遠入朝，更名從阮，置永安軍於府州，以從阮為節度使。

translations.literal: Zhenwu military governor and Fuzhou training commissioner She Congyuan entered court, changed his name to Congruan, established Yong'an Army at Fuzhou, and made Congruan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: She Congyuan of Zhenwu and Fuzhou came to court, renamed himself Congruan, established the Yong'an command at Fuzhou, and made him its governor.

sentences.zh: 又以河東左都押牙劉銖為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: He also made Hedong left chief military aide Liu Zhu Heyang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Liu Zhu of Hedong governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 銖，陝人也。

translations.literal: Zhu was a man of Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was from Shaan.

sentences.zh: 契丹昭義節度使耿崇美屯澤州，將攻潞州。

translations.literal: Khitan Zhaoyi military governor Geng Chongmei encamped at Ze Prefecture and was about to attack Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Chongmei of Zhaoyi camped at Zezhou and prepared to attack Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔史弘肇將步騎萬人救之。

translations.literal: On yichou, an edict ordered Shi Hongzhao to lead ten thousand infantry and cavalry to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the emperor ordered Shi Hongzhao to march ten thousand foot and horse to the relief.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以王守恩為昭義節度使，高允權為彰武節度使，又以岢嵐軍使鄭廉為忻州刺史，領彰國節度使兼忻、代二州義軍都部署。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Wang Shou'en was made Zhaoyi military governor; Gao Yunquan Zhangwu military governor; also Kelan Army commander Zheng Lian Xizhou prefect, holding Zhangguo military governor with concurrent overall deployment of righteous armies of Xi and Dai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Wang Shou'en was made governor of Zhaoyi, Gao Yunquan of Zhangwu; Zheng Lian of Kelan was made prefect of Xinzhou and governor of Zhangguo with command of the Xi and Dai righteous armies.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以緣河巡檢使閻萬進為嵐州刺史，領振武節度使兼嵐、憲二州義軍都制置使。

translations.literal: On dingmao, River-border inspection commissioner Yan Wanjin was made Lanzhou prefect, holding Zhenwu military governor with concurrent overall disposition of righteous armies of Lan and Xian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Yan Wanjin, river-border inspector, was made prefect of Lanzhou and governor of Zhenwu with command of the Lan and Xian righteous armies.

sentences.zh: 帝聞契丹北歸，欲經略河南，故以弘肇為前驅，又遣謙萬進出北方以分契丹兵勢。

translations.literal: The emperor heard the Khitan were returning north and wished to plan for the region south of the river; therefore he made Hongzhao the vanguard, and also sent Lian and Wanjin out to the north to divide Khitan military momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the Khitan were going north, the emperor planned to recover the central plains, sent Hongzhao as vanguard, and posted Lian and Wanjin northward to divide Khitan strength.

sentences.zh: 萬進，并州人也。

translations.literal: Wanjin was a man of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjin was from Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹主以船數十艘載晉鎧仗，將自汴溯河歸其國，命寧國都虞候榆次武行德將士卒千餘人部送之。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor used several dozen ships to carry Jin armor and weapons, intending from Bian to go upriver homeward, and ordered Ningguo chief adjutant Wu Xingde of Yuci to lead more than a thousand soldiers and officers to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor loaded dozens of ships with Jin arms to sail upriver from Bian homeward, with Wu Xingde of Yuci escorting a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 至河陰，行德與將士謀曰：「今為虜所制，將遠去鄉里。

translations.literal: Reaching Heyin, Xingde plotted with officers and soldiers: "Now we are controlled by the barbarians and will go far from our home districts.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin, Xingde told his men, "We are prisoners of the barbarians, bound for a foreign land.

sentences.zh: 人生會有死，安能為異域之鬼乎！

translations.literal: Human life surely has death—how can we become ghosts in a foreign land!
translations.idiomatic: Men must die—how can we become ghosts in a foreign land!

sentences.zh: 虜勢不能久留中國，不若共逐其黨，堅守河陽，以俟天命之所歸者而臣之，豈非長策乎！」

translations.literal: The barbarians' momentum cannot long remain in China—better together to drive off their party, firmly hold Heyang, and wait for whom heaven's mandate returns to and serve him—is this not the long stratagem!"
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians cannot stay long in China—let us drive them off, hold Heyang, and serve whoever heaven chooses—is that not the wise course!

sentences.zh: 眾以為然。

translations.literal: The crowd thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed.

sentences.zh: 行德即以鎧仗授之，相與殺契丹監軍使。

translations.literal: Xingde immediately gave them the armor and weapons; together they killed the Khitan army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde armed them and together they killed the Khitan supervisor.

sentences.zh: 會契丹河陽節度使崔廷勳以兵送耿崇美之潞州，行德遂乘虛入據河陽，眾推行德為河陽都部署。

translations.literal: It happened that Khitan Heyang military governor Cui Tingxun was escorting Geng Chongmei to Lu Prefecture with troops; Xingde thereupon seized the opening to enter and hold Heyang; the crowd elevated Xingde as Heyang overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tingxun of Heyang was escorting Geng Chongmei to Luzhou; Xingde seized Heyang and the troops made him overall commander.

sentences.zh: 行德遣弟行友奉蠟表間道詣晉陽。

translations.literal: Xingde sent his younger brother Xingyou with a sealed memorial by a hidden route to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde sent his brother Xingyou by a secret route to Jinyang with a sealed memorial.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣武定節度使方太詣洛陽巡檢，至鄭州。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent Wuding military governor Fang Tai to Luoyang for inspection; he reached Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent Fang Tai of Wuding to inspect Luoyang; he reached Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 州有戍兵，共迫太為鄭王。

translations.literal: The prefecture had garrison troops who together compelled Tai to be Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison troops forced him to become Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 梁嗣密王朱乙逃禍為僧，嵩山賊帥張遇得之，立以為天子，取嵩岳神袞冕以衣之，帥眾萬餘襲鄭州，太擊走之。

translations.literal: Liang heir Prince of Simi Zhu Yi fled disaster as a monk; Song Mountain bandit chief Zhang Yu obtained him, established him as Son of Heaven, took Mount Song spirit robes and crown to clothe him, and led a force of more than ten thousand to raid Zheng Prefecture; Tai struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi, heir prince of Simi, had fled as a monk; bandit chief Zhang Yu of Mount Song made him emperor, dressed him in sacred robes from Mount Song, and led ten thousand men against Zhengzhou; Tai drove them off.

sentences.zh: 太以契丹尚強，恐事不濟，說諭戍兵，欲與之俱西，眾不從，太自西門逃奔洛陽。

translations.literal: Tai, because the Khitan were still strong, feared matters would not succeed, persuaded and instructed the garrison troops, wishing to go west with them; the crowd did not follow; Tai himself fled through the west gate to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Khitan were still too strong, Tai tried to persuade the garrison to march west with him; they refused, and he fled through the west gate to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 戍兵既失太，反譖太於契丹，雲脅我為亂。

translations.literal: After the garrison had lost Tai, they in turn slandered Tai to the Khitan, saying he coerced them into rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: After he fled, the garrison slandered him to the Khitan, claiming he had forced them into rebellion.

sentences.zh: 太遣子師朗自訴於契丹，契丹將麻荅殺之，太無以自明。

translations.literal: Tai sent his son Shilang to plead his own case to the Khitan; Khitan general Mada killed him; Tai had no way to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tai sent his son Shilang to plead his case; the Khitan general Mada killed him, and Tai could not clear his name.

sentences.zh: 會群盜攻洛陽，契丹留守劉晞棄城奔許州，太乃入府行留守事，與巡檢使潘環擊群盜卻之，張遇殺朱乙請降。

translations.literal: It happened that bandit groups attacked Luoyang; Khitan garrison commander Liu Xi abandoned the city and fled to Xu Prefecture; Tai then entered the headquarters to conduct garrison affairs, with inspection commissioner Pan Huan struck bandit groups and repelled them; Zhang Yu killed Zhu Yi and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits attacked Luoyang; Liu Xi abandoned the city for Xuzhou; Tai took over as acting commander, and with Pan Huan repelled the bandits; Zhang Yu killed Zhu Yi and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 伊闕賊帥自稱天子，誓眾於南郊壇，將入洛陽，太逆擊，走之。

translations.literal: A Yique bandit chief declared himself Son of Heaven, swore the crowd at the southern suburban altar, was about to enter Luoyang; Tai counterattacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: A bandit chief at Yique declared himself emperor and swore his men at the southern suburban altar before marching on Luoyang; Tai routed him.

sentences.zh: 太欲自歸於晉陽，武行德使人誘太曰：「我裨校也，公舊鎮此地，今虛位相待。」

translations.literal: Tai wished to submit himself to Jinyang; Wu Xingde sent someone to entice Tai: "I am a lieutenant—you once governed this place; now an empty seat awaits you."
translations.idiomatic: Tai wished to submit to Jinyang; Wu Xingde sent word: "I am your subordinate—you once held this post, and the seat awaits you."

sentences.zh: 太信之，至河陽，為行德所殺。

translations.literal: Tai believed it; reaching Heyang, he was killed by Xingde.
translations.idiomatic: Tai believed him; reaching Heyang, Xingde killed him.

sentences.zh: 蕭翰遣高謨翰援送劉晞自許還洛陽，晞疑潘環構其眾逐己，使謨翰殺之。

translations.literal: Xiao Han sent Gao Mohan to escort Liu Xi from Xu back to Luoyang; Xi suspected Pan Huan had engineered his crowd to expel him and had Mohan kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Han sent Gao Mohan to escort Liu Xi from Xu back to Luoyang; Xi suspected Pan Huan had turned the troops against him and had Mohan kill Pan.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，武行友至晉陽。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Wu Xingyou reached Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Wu Xingyou reached Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 庚午，史弘肇奏遣先鋒將馬誨擊契丹，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Shi Hongzhao memorialized sending vanguard general Ma Hui to strike the Khitan, beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Shi Hongzhao reported that vanguard Ma Hui had struck the Khitan and taken more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 時耿崇美，崔廷勳至澤州，聞弘肇兵已入潞州，不敢進，引眾而南。

translations.literal: At the time Geng Chongmei and Cui Tingxun reached Ze Prefecture; hearing Hongzhao's troops had already entered Lu Prefecture, they dared not advance and led their crowd south.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Chongmei and Cui Tingxun had reached Zezhou; hearing Hongzhao had entered Luzhou, they dared not advance and withdrew south.

sentences.zh: 弘肇遣誨追擊，破之，崇美、廷勳與奚王拽剌退保懷州。

translations.literal: Hongzhao sent Hui in pursuit, defeated them; Chongmei, Tingxun, and Xi king Zhuaici withdrew to defend Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao sent Hui in pursuit, routed them, and Chongmei, Tingxun, and Xi king Zhuaici fell back to Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以武行德為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Wu Xingde was made Heyang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Wu Xingde was made governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 契丹主聞河陽亂，歎曰：「我有三失，宜天下之叛我也！

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor heard of turmoil at Heyang and sighed: "I had three failures—it is fitting that all under heaven rebelled against me!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the revolt at Heyang, the Khitan emperor sighed, "I made three mistakes—no wonder the realm turned against me!

sentences.zh: 諸道括錢，一失也；

translations.literal: Forced loans in the circuits—one failure;
translations.idiomatic: Forced loans in every circuit—that was the first;

sentences.zh: 令上國人打草穀，二失也；

translations.literal: ordering northerners to 'beat the grass for grain'—two failures;
translations.idiomatic: letting my people loot as 'beating the grass for grain'—the second;

sentences.zh: 不早遣諸節度使還鎮，三失也。」

translations.literal: not early sending the military governors back to their posts—three failures."
translations.idiomatic: and not sending the governors back to their posts sooner—the third."

sentences.zh: 唐主以矯詔敗軍，皆陳覺、馮延魯之罪，壬申，詔赦諸將，議斬二人以謝中外。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler held that the forged edict and defeated army were all the crimes of Chen Jue and Feng Yanlu. On renshen, an edict pardoned the generals and deliberated beheading the two men to apologize inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Blaming the forged edict and defeated army on Chen Jue and Feng Yanlu, the Tang emperor on renshen pardoned the generals and debated executing the two men to appease court and realm.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞江文蔚對仗彈馮延己、魏岑曰：「陛下踐阼以來，所信任者，延己、延魯、岑、覺四人而已，皆陰狡弄權，壅蔽聰明，排斥忠良，引用群小，諫爭者逐，竊議者刑，上下相蒙，道路以目。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Jiang Wenwei, facing the throne, impeached Feng Yanji and Wei Qin, saying: "Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, those you have trusted are only Yanji, Yanlu, Qin, and Jue—four men only—all secretly crafty in wielding power, blocking and obscuring your clarity, expelling the loyal and good, employing petty men, remonstrators expelled, private discussers punished, above and below deceiving one another, and on the roads people cover their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Jiang Wenwei impeached Feng Yanji and Wei Qin at court: "Since Your Majesty took the throne you have trusted only Yanji, Yanlu, Qin, and Jue—four men who secretly manipulate power, blind your judgment, drive out the loyal, elevate petty men, exile remonstrators, punish whisperers, and leave the realm afraid to speak.

sentences.zh: 今覺、延魯雖伏辜，而延己、岑猶在，本根未殄，枝幹復生。

translations.literal: Now Jue and Yanlu though have paid guilt, yet Yanji and Qin remain—the root is not exterminated, branches and stems will grow again.
translations.idiomatic: Jue and Yanlu are punished, but Yanji and Qin remain—the root is not cut, and the branches will grow again.

sentences.zh: 同罪異誅，人心疑惑。」

translations.literal: Same crime, different executions—people's hearts are doubtful."
translations.idiomatic: Equal guilt but unequal punishment breeds doubt.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「上之視聽，惟在數人，雖日接群臣，終成孤立。」

translations.literal: He also said: "What the ruler sees and hears rests only in a few men; though daily receiving the hundred ministers, in the end he becomes isolated."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Your eyes and ears rest on a few men; though you meet ministers daily, you stand alone.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「在外者握兵，居中者當國。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Those outside hold troops; those at the center manage the state."
translations.idiomatic: Those abroad hold armies; those at the center run the state.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「岑、覺、延魯，更相違戾，彼前則我卻，彼東則我西。

translations.literal: He also said: "Qin, Jue, and Yanlu oppose one another in turn—when they advance, I retreat; when they go east, I go west.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, Jue, and Yanlu feud with one another—when one advances, another retreats; when one goes east, another goes west.

sentences.zh: 天生五材，國之利器，一旦為小人忿爭妄動之具。」

translations.literal: Heaven born five materials, the state's sharp tools—in one morning they became instruments for petty men's angry quarrels and reckless movements."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gave five talents to serve the state—yet they became tools for petty men's quarrels.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「征討之柄，在岑折簡，帑藏取與，系岑一言。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The handle of campaigns rests in Qin's folded note; treasury taking and giving hangs on one word from Qin."
translations.idiomatic: The power to wage war rests in Qin's folded note; treasury disbursements hang on his word.

sentences.zh: 唐主以文蔚所言為太過，怒，貶江州司士參軍。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler thought Wenwei's words excessive, was angry, and demoted him to Jiangzhou registrar aide.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor thought Wenwei had gone too far, grew angry, and demoted him to registrar aide at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 械送覺、延魯至金陵。

translations.literal: Jue and Yanlu were sent in shackles to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Jue and Yanlu were sent in chains to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 宋齊丘以嘗薦覺使福州，上表待罪。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu, because he had once recommended Jue as envoy to Fuzhou, submitted a memorial awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu, who had once recommended Jue for the Fuzhou mission, submitted a confession.

sentences.zh: 詔流覺於蘄州，延魯於舒州。

translations.literal: An edict exiled Jue to Qizhou and Yanlu to Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exiled Jue to Qizhou and Yanlu to Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 知制誥會稽徐鉉、史館修撰韓熙載上疏曰：「覺、延魯罪不容誅，但齊丘、延己為之陳請，故陛下赦之。

translations.literal: Drafting edict officer Xu Xuan of Kuaiji and Historiography Compiler Han Xizai submitted a memorial saying: "Jue and Yanlu's crimes could not bear mere execution, but Qiqiu and Yanji pleaded for them, so Your Majesty pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuan of Kuaiji and Han Xizai memorialized: "Jue and Yanlu deserved death, but Qiqiu and Yanji pleaded for them, so Your Majesty spared them.

sentences.zh: 擅興者不罪，則疆場有生事者矣；

translations.literal: If those who rashly raise armies are not punished, then on the borders there will be those who stir trouble;
translations.idiomatic: If those who launch wars unpunished go free, the frontiers will breed trouble;

sentences.zh: 喪師者獲存，則行陳無效死者矣。

translations.literal: if those who lose armies are preserved, then in the battle lines there will be none who die effectively.
translations.idiomatic: if defeated commanders survive, no soldier will die trying.

sentences.zh: 請行顯戮以重軍威。」

translations.literal: I request open execution to weight army prestige."
translations.idiomatic: Execute them publicly to restore military discipline."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事馮延己罷為太弟少保，貶魏岑為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Secretariat Attendant and Grand Councilor Feng Yanji was removed to Junior Mentor of the Imperial Younger Brother; Wei Qin was demoted to Crown Prince's Stable Groom.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanji was demoted from grand councilor to junior mentor of the imperial younger brother; Wei Qin was reduced to crown prince's stable groom.

sentences.zh: 韓熙載屢言宋齊丘黨與必為禍亂。

translations.literal: Han Xizai repeatedly said Song Qiqiu's faction would surely bring calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xizai repeatedly warned that Song Qiqiu's faction would bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 齊丘奏熙載嗜酒猖狂，貶和州司士參軍。

translations.literal: Qiqiu memorialized that Xizai was addicted to wine and wildly arrogant, and demoted him to Hezhou registrar aide.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu accused Xizai of drunken arrogance and had him demoted to registrar aide at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，鳳州防禦使石奉頵舉州降蜀。

translations.literal: On yihai, Feng Prefecture defense commissioner Shi Fengyun raised the prefecture and surrendered to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Shi Fengyun of Fengzhou surrendered the prefecture to Shu.

sentences.zh: 奉頵，晉之宗屬也。

translations.literal: Fengyun was a clansman of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyun was a member of the Jin imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 契丹主至臨城，得疾，及欒城，病甚，苦熱，聚冰於胸腹手足，且啖之。

translations.literal: The Khitan emperor reached Lincheng and fell ill; reaching Luancheng his illness was severe; he suffered from heat, gathered ice on chest, belly, hands, and feet, and even ate it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor fell ill at Lincheng; at Luancheng he grew desperately hot, packed ice on his chest, belly, hands, and feet, and even ate it.

sentences.zh: 丙子，至殺胡林而卒。

translations.literal: On bingzi he reached Kill-Barbarian Forest and died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi he died at Kill-Barbarian Forest.

sentences.zh: 國人剖其腹，實鹽數鬥，載之北去，晉人謂之「帝□」。

translations.literal: His countrymen cut open his belly, filled it with several pecks of salt, and carried him north; Jin people called him "Emperor [taboo character]."
translations.idiomatic: His followers gutted him, packed his belly with pecks of salt, and carried the corpse north; Jin subjects called him the "Salted Emperor."

sentences.zh: 趙延壽恨契丹主負約，謂人曰：「我不復入龍沙矣。」

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou resented the Khitan emperor's broken promise and said to people: "I will not again enter Dragon Sands."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou, bitter that the Khitan emperor had broken his word, said, "I will never return to the northern desert."

sentences.zh: 即日，先引兵入恆州，契丹永康王兀欲及南北二王，各以所部兵相繼而入。

translations.literal: That same day he first led troops into Heng Prefecture; Khitan Prince of Yongkang Wuyu and the northern and southern kings each with their own troops entered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he marched into Hengzhou first; Prince Yongkang Wuyu and the northern and southern kings followed with their troops.

sentences.zh: 延壽欲拒之，恐失大援，乃納之。

translations.literal: Yanshou wished to refuse them but feared losing great support, and thereupon admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou wanted to refuse them but feared losing Khitan support and let them in.

sentences.zh: 時契丹諸將已密議奉兀欲為主，兀欲登鼓角樓受叔兄拜。

translations.literal: At the time Khitan generals had already secretly deliberated to elevate Wuyu as ruler; Wuyu ascended the drum and horn tower to receive his uncle-elders' bows.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan generals had already secretly agreed to make Wuyu ruler; he mounted the drum tower to receive the elders' homage.

sentences.zh: 而延壽不之知，自稱受契丹皇帝遺詔，權知南朝軍國事，仍下教佈告諸道，所以供給兀欲與諸將同，兀欲銜之。

translations.literal: Yet Yanshou did not know this, declared himself to have received the Khitan emperor's testamentary edict, and acted as temporary manager of the southern dynasty's military and state affairs, still issuing instructions and proclaiming them to the circuits. The supplies given Wuyu were the same as the generals'; Wuyu harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou knew nothing of this and proclaimed himself regent of the southern realm by the late emperor's will, issuing orders to every circuit. He gave Wuyu no more than he gave other generals, and Wuyu resented it.

sentences.zh: 恆州諸門管鑰及倉庫出納，兀欲皆自主之。

translations.literal: Heng Prefecture's gate keys and treasury receipts and disbursements—Wuyu controlled them all himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu seized every gate key and treasury receipt in Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 延壽使人請之，不與。

translations.literal: Yanshou sent someone to request them; he would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshou sent to request them, Wuyu refused.

sentences.zh: 契丹主喪至國，述律太后不哭，曰：「待諸部寧壹如故，則葬汝矣。」

translations.literal: When the Khitan emperor's coffin reached the state, Empress Dowager Shulü did not weep and said: "Wait until the various tribes are calm and united as before—then I will bury you."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor's coffin reached home, Empress Dowager Shulü did not weep. "When the tribes are calm again," she said, "then I will bury you."

sentences.zh: 帝之自壽陽還也，留兵千人戍承天軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Shouyang, he left a thousand troops to garrison Chengtian Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Shouyang he left a thousand men to garrison Chengtian Army.

sentences.zh: 戍兵聞契丹北還，不為備。

translations.literal: The garrison troops heard the Khitan had returned north and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison, hearing the Khitan had gone north, took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 契丹襲擊之，戍兵驚潰；

translations.literal: The Khitan raided them; the garrison troops fled in alarm;
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan struck; the garrison broke in panic;

sentences.zh: 契丹焚其市邑，一日狼煙百餘舉。

translations.literal: the Khitan burned their market towns; in one day wolf smoke rose more than a hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: the Khitan burned the market towns and raised more than a hundred beacon fires in a day.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此虜將遁，張虛勢也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "These barbarians are about to flee—they are spreading false momentum."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The barbarians are about to flee—they are bluffing.

sentences.zh: 遣親將葉仁魯將步騎三千赴之。

translations.literal: He sent intimate general Ye Renlu to lead three thousand infantry and cavalry there.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his trusted general Ye Renlu with three thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 會契丹出剽掠，仁魯乘虛大破之，丁丑，復取承天軍。

translations.literal: It happened the Khitan went out plundering; Renlu seized the opening and routed them greatly; on dingchou he recovered Chengtian Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan went out to loot, Renlu struck their camp and routed them; on dingchou he retook Chengtian Army.

sentences.zh: 冀州人殺契丹刺史何行通，推牢城指揮使張廷翰知州事。

translations.literal: The people of Ji Prefecture killed Khitan prefect He Xingtong and elevated Laocheng commander Zhang Tinghan to handle prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jizhou killed the Khitan prefect He Xingtong and made Zhang Tinghan of Laocheng acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 廷翰，冀州人，符習之甥也。

translations.literal: Tinghan was a man of Ji Prefecture, nephew of Fu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghan was from Jizhou, nephew of Fu Xi.

sentences.zh: 或說趙延壽曰：「契丹諸大人數日聚謀，此必有變。

translations.literal: Someone said to Zhao Yanshou: "Khitan great men have gathered for several days in counsel—there must be a change.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Zhao Yanshou, "The Khitan lords have met in secret for days—something is brewing.

sentences.zh: 今漢兵不減萬人，不若先事圖之。」

translations.literal: Now Han troops are not fewer than ten thousand—better to act first and plan against it."
translations.idiomatic: You still have ten thousand Han troops—strike first."

sentences.zh: 延壽猶豫不決。

translations.literal: Yanshou hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou hesitated.

sentences.zh: 壬午，延壽下令，以來月朔日於待賢館上事，受文武官賀。

translations.literal: On renwu Yanshou issued an order that on the first day of the coming month he would conduct affairs at the Lodge of Awaiting the Worthy and receive civil and military officials' congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Yanshou ordered that on the first of next month he would hold court at the Lodge of Awaiting the Worthy and receive officials' congratulations.

sentences.zh: 其儀：宰相、樞密使拜於階上，節度使以下拜於階下。

translations.literal: The ceremony: chancellors and commissioner of military affairs bowed on the steps above; military governors and below bowed on the steps below.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors and the commissioner of military affairs would bow on the upper steps; governors and below on the lower.

sentences.zh: 李崧以虜意不同，事理難測，固請趙延壽未行此禮，乃止。

translations.literal: Li Song, because barbarian intent differed and matters were hard to fathom, firmly requested Zhao Yanshou not carry out this ceremony, and only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song, fearing unpredictable Khitan reactions, strongly urged Yanshou to abandon the ceremony, and he did.
